# Self-check questions

Try each question before you read the answer key. The label at the end of each question names the chapter that answers it (two chapters for questions 14 and 15). Most questions need a number from the repositories as well as an explanation.

1. Rev A's tip moves at 2.5 km/s on an arm 320 km long (`params/rev_a.json`). Work out the spin period and the tip acceleration in g. Then explain why an accelerometer on a payload just caught at the lower tip reads about 2.07 g, not canon's 1.99 g. (Chapter A2)

2. From the CoM altitude, half-length, tip speed and μ in `params/rev_a.json`, plus the code's mean Earth radius of 6,371 km, compute the release speed, C3 and apogee altitude of the 2.5 km/s throw. Why is the release point the perigee of the new orbit, and why does the result rule out calling the reference throw "cislunar"? (Chapter A3)

3. How much energy does each kilogram gain in one Rev A throw, and why is the 37.78 MJ/kg in the finance code too low? How much reboost power does canon's cadence of 1 catch per day need, and how does that compare with the founding document's "100 kW–1 MW" claim? (Chapter A5)

4. The glossary gives Rev A's taper ratio as about 8.2, yet the conservative tether weighs 121.83 times its payload. Why are these different quantities, which taper goes with 121.83×, and how much fibre does the conservative case need for a 5 t payload? (Chapter A6)

5. The finance Monte Carlo reports P(payback by Y15) = 75.2% from 10,000 seeded draws. How large is its sampling error, and why would 100,000 draws not make the figure much more trustworthy? (Chapter A8)

6. Show from the Conservative inputs why the break-even customer price is $550.11/kg. Why is NPV at a 10% discount rate still negative at that price? (Chapter A9)

7. A `porkchop_scan` best cell reports `vInfDep` = 8.0337 km/s and `c3` = 64.54 km²/s². Show how the two are related, and give the departure speeds that match Aster's 25 km²/s² "low C3" cut and its 0.1 km²/s² near-zero flag. Why is Apophis's catalog-best C3 of 0.000206 km²/s² not a cheap mission? (Chapter B1)

8. The published MCP server, `aster-mission-mcp@0.1.0`, says its Earth ephemeris span is "2025-12-31 through 2040-12-30", yet it refuses a departure on 2025-12-31. Use the TDB − UTC offset to explain both halves, and say what `main` changed. (Chapter B2)

9. Why does a single-revolution (M = 0) Lambert problem have exactly one solution for any positive flight time, while an M = 2 problem can have none or two? Use the fourth cell of the pinned Apophis fixture (Δt = 57,339,026.794 s, M = 2) to show the "none" case. (Chapter B5)

10. For the Apophis cell departing 2028-06-01 with a 300-day flight on Falcon Heavy Expendable (C3 = 2.46685 km²/s², arrival v∞ = 4.08943 km/s), compute the delivered mass. Why would adding the 3.336 km/s injection burn to the spacecraft's Δv budget be wrong? (Chapter B7)

11. In the Slice 16 study, Sonnet passed FULL faithfulness on 30 of 126 graded runs. A Wilson 95% interval gives about [17%, 32%], but the study reports [6.1%, 45.6%]. Why is the reported interval almost three times wider, and which one is honest? (Chapter B11)

12. The 2.8 km/s tier releases a payload at C3 = −1.94 km²/s², still bound to Earth. Why can it still put almost four times as much mass on a C3 = 5 km²/s² departure as a burn from a 200 km LEO, starting from the same 5,000 kg stack? (Chapter C1)

13. Even when a skyhook supplies exactly the right C3, an equatorial tether can cost a probe a large share of its arrived mass. Why, how large is the loss in the unmerged PM-001 study, and why can Aster's own launch-site model not price it? (Chapter C1)

14. A correct number can still do damage if its label is lost. Use Skyhook's 440× mass ratio and Aster's `estimate_mission_cost` envelope for 433 Eros to show this. In the Eros case, what does the top-level confidence "assumed" tell you, and what does it not? (Chapter A11 and Chapter B10)

15. A green test run is not proof that the numbers are right. Give one example from each repository where a passing step or a passing count hides something, with the numbers. (Chapter A12 and Chapter B8)

## Answer key

**1.** Spin rate, period and load follow from tip speed and arm length alone (Section A2.8):

```
ω = v_tip / L     = 2.5 / 320                  = 0.0078125 rad/s
T = 2πL / v_tip   = 2,010.62 km / 2.5 km/s     = 804.25 s = 13.40 min
a = v_tip² / L    = 2,500² / 320,000           = 19.53 m/s² = 1.99 g
felt at catch     = 19.53 + (8.984 − 8.179)    = 20.34 m/s² = 2.07 g
```

`rotation_period_min()` and `tip_acceleration_g()` in skyhook: `physics/skyhook_physics.py` return 13.404 min and 1.9916 g [Certain]. Canon's 1.99 g is the centripetal term only. The lower tip is 320 km below the free-falling hub, where gravity is 0.805 m/s² stronger, so the tether must pull that much harder and the payload feels about 2.07 g, 4% more [Certain as arithmetic] (Section A2.10). The unmerged catch-window study (branch `claude/creative-catch-window-lab`, `docs/research/cw001_catch_window.md`) reaches the same 2.07 g.

**2.** The energy must be evaluated at the tip radius, 7,301 km (Section A3.12):

```
v_rel = √(398,600 / 6,981) + 2.5        = 7.5563 + 2.5        = 10.0563 km/s
ε     = 10.0563² / 2 − 398,600 / 7,301  = 50.5647 − 54.5953   = −4.0306 km²/s²
C3    = 2ε                                                    = −8.06 km²/s²
a     = 398,600 / 8.0611 = 49,447 km;   r_apo = 2a − 7,301    = 91,593 km
apogee altitude = 91,593 − 6,371                              = 85,222 km
```

`apogee_from_release(2.5)` in skyhook: `physics/skyhook_physics.py` returns C3 = −8.0611 and 85,222.33 km, matching `params/rev_a.json` `kinematics` [Certain]. At the top of the swing the velocity is purely horizontal, so the point is an apsis; 10.056 km/s is faster than the local circular speed of 7.389 km/s, so the payload climbs from there, which makes it the perigee, at 930 km altitude. A negative C3 means a bound orbit: high-elliptical, GTO class, with an apogee radius about 2.2 times GEO's, nowhere near the Moon (`docs/DECISION_LOG.md` §4 records the correction). Lunar distance needs the 2.8 km/s tier, apogee altitude 397,819 km (`params/rev_a.json` `cislunar_revenue_gated_option`). Do not start from canon's `orbital.com_radius_km` = 6,988: it is 610 + 6,378 (equatorial radius), no code reads it, and every calculation uses 6,981 km (Section A3.3). The test `tests/test_rev_a_physics.py::test_reference_upper_release_is_cislunar_not_escape` is misnamed and checks escape speed at the CoM radius, a looser bar (Section A3.10).

**3.** The full gain is the change in orbital energy from catch to release (Sections A5.7 and A5.15):

```
full gain     Δε = ε_release − ε_catch = −4.0306 − (−47.0577) = 43.03 MJ/kg
finance       2 · v_orb · v_tip = 2 × 7.5563 × 2.5            = 37.78 MJ/kg  (kinetic only)
missing climb 6,661 km → 7,301 km                             =  5.25 MJ/kg  (13.9% of 37.78)
power         5,000 kg × 43.03 MJ/kg / 86,400 s               =  2.49 MW to the orbit
electrical    2.49 MW / 0.15                                  = 16.6 MW
```

`marginal_cost_per_kg()` in skyhook: `finance/skyhook_finance.py` counts only the kinetic-energy gain and leaves out the climb from catch radius to release radius [Certain]. In dollars the gap is only +$0.78/kg at the Conservative rung, but a power budget built on 37.78 MJ/kg comes out 12.2% too small (the true need is 13.9% larger). At 1 MW electrical and 15% efficiency only 0.15 MW reaches the orbit, so one throw takes 16.6 days to repay: the claim in `docs/project_instructions.md` §4.6 is about 17 times short, and the array alone would weigh 166–332 t at 100–50 W/kg [Certain arithmetic; efficiency Likely].

**4.** The two equations measure different things (Sections A6.7 and A6.9):

```
x² = (v_tip / V_c)² × SF / (1 − d) = (2.5 / 2.7269)² × 2.5 / 0.70 = 3.0018
EQ-5 taper (area, hub ÷ tip)       = e^(x²)                         = 20.12
EQ-6 mass ratio (both arms)        = 2√π · x · e^(x²) · erf(x)      = 121.83
fibre                              = 121.83 × 5,000 kg              = 609.1 t
```

EQ-5 is a peak cross-section ratio, and that peak exists only near the hub; EQ-6 adds up the mass along both arms, which also depends on the tip area the payload sets [Certain]. `taper_ratio()` in skyhook: `physics/skyhook_physics.py` has no derate argument, so the glossary's ~8.2 (8.18) belongs to the 0% derate tether, which pairs with 40.32×; the 30% derate tether that pairs with 121.83× has a taper of 20.12. Treating EQ-5 as a mass ratio was the project's own recorded error (`docs/DECISION_LOG.md` §2): doubled for two arms it gives 16.4, a different quantity, not a rough version of 121.83 (Section A6.10). The 121.83× and 609.1 t are canon in `params/rev_a.json` `mass_ratio` [Certain].

**5.** Sampling error is already small (Section A8.7):

```
SE = √( p (1 − p) / N ) = √(0.7525 × 0.2475 / 10,000) = 0.0043   →   95% band ≈ ±0.85 points
```

Re-runs with seeds 1 to 10 gave 74.45% to 76.00%, as predicted, and more draws only shrink this noise as 1/√N [Certain]. The large uncertainties are ones sampling cannot see: the eight input triangles in skyhook: `finance/sensitivity.py` are self-set and [Speculative], and centring them on the Conservative values drops the result to about 33% (Section A8.15). One price–cadence correlation moves it between 70.5% and 82.5%, and the model has no demand variable: every draw sells at least 727 t/yr, while any demand cap at or below 800 t/yr gives 0% (Section A8.16) [Certain arithmetic for these guide-computed variants]. More draws make the number more repeatable, not more true.

**6.** The break-even price recovers all costs by Y15 over the effective kilograms sold (Section A9.12):

```
p* = (capex + fixed × 11 + variable × 9.9) / (upmass × 9.9)
   = (8,741.09 + 80 × 11 + 32.115 × 9.9) $M / (1,825,000 kg × 9.9)
   = 9,939.03 $M / 18,067,500 kg = $550.11/kg
```

`breakeven_customer_price_y15()` in skyhook: `finance/skyhook_finance.py` makes cumulative undiscounted cash zero at Y15; the 11 operating years count as 9.9 full years because of the 0.3 and 0.6 ramp [Certain]. No discount factor appears, so heavy early spending and late income are not penalised: at $550.11/kg the Conservative NPV@10% is still about −$3,537M, and the price that zeroes the 15-year NPV@10% is about $1,063/kg (computed for the guide). The `COMPARABILITY_WARNING` in `finance/export_grid.py` wrongly says the break-even comes from discounted cash flows (Section A9.13).

**7.** C3 is the square of the departure excess speed (Section B1.9.4):

```
C3 = v∞²:         8.033724² = 64.5407 km²/s²
low-C3 cut:       √25       = 5.00 km/s
near-zero flag:   √0.1      = 0.316 km/s   (316 m/s)
Apophis best:     √0.000206 = 0.0144 km/s  (about 14 m/s)
```

The thresholds sit in aster: `src/v2/app/catalog-list/honesty-disclosure.ts` (25) and `src/v2/core/constants/near-zero-c3.ts` (0.1) [Certain]. Apophis's best window (depart 2028-09-14, 212 days) leaves Earth at only 14 m/s because Earth and Apophis are about 45,900 km apart at the arrival instant: the "spacecraft" barely leaves Earth's orbit, and Apophis flies past at 5.84 km/s, which a rendezvous would have to cancel [numbers Certain; interpretation Likely] (Section B1.3). Aster's disclosure calls such values "mathematically valid but operationally meaningless", and the Slice 18 fidelity file supports Apophis screening only through 2028-09-12, before this window (`tools/slice18-research/tier-sizing-per-body.json`). The published package's `get_body` returns the number with neither a near-zero flag nor a tier.

**8.** A TDB midnight is 69.184 s before the UTC midnight of the same date (Sections B2.7 and B2.8):

```
TDB − UTC = 37 s + 32.184 s = 69.184 s
first record JD(TDB) 2461041.5 = 2026-01-01 00:00 TDB = 2025-12-31T23:58:50.816Z → label "2025-12-31"
UTC midnight 2025-12-31        = JD(TDB) 2461040.500800741 < 2461041.5           → refused
```

The ephemeris aster: `src/v2/data/horizons-inner-solar-system-2026-2040.json` starts at TDB midnight, and `jdTdbToUtcDateString` in `mcp/src/tools/compute-shared.ts` keeps the first 10 characters of the converted UTC time, so it prints "2025-12-31" [Certain]. The refusal itself is correct: UTC midnight on 2025-12-31 is almost a day before the first record. On `main`, `acceptedUtcDateBounds` moves a rendered bound one day inward when its UTC midnight would be refused, so the window reads 2026-01-01 through 2040-12-30 [Likely: read in code, not run]. That fix (commit `0052ecb`, 2026-09-23; Section B10.9) is unpublished, because 0.1.0 is still the only release.

**9.** The answer is in the shape of the time-of-flight curve T(x) (Sections B5.6 and B5.9):

```
M ≥ 1:  T(x; M) = T(x; 0) + Mπ / (1 − x²)^(3/2)     U-shaped, lowest point T_min(M)
T_min(M = 2) = 63,710,029.77 s (737.38 days)
57,339,026.794 / 63,710,029.771 = 0.900   →   T* = 6.991 < T_min = 7.768   →   null
```

For M = 0, Izzo's T(x) only falls as x rises, so a horizontal line at the required time T* crosses it exactly once [Certain]. For M ≥ 1 the extra term grows without limit as x → −1 and x → +1, so below T_min no M-lap orbit exists and above it the line cuts the U twice, giving the left and right branches (aster: `src/v2/core/lambert/lambert-multi-rev.ts`). The fixture aster: `tests/fixtures/v2/lambert-multi-rev-pinned-cells.json` sets its fourth cell at exactly 0.9 × T_min(M = 2), so `lambertMultiRev` must return `null` and the fixture expects `ok: false` [Certain] (Section B5.10).

**10.** Interpolate the payload, then apply the rocket equation to the spacecraft's own burns (Sections B7.14 and B7.16):

```
payload at C3 = 15,010 + 0.246685 × (12,345 − 15,010)   = 14,352.58 kg
Δv_sc         = 4,089.43 + 0.05 × 4,089.43 + 150        = 4,443.90 m/s
v_e           = 320 s × 9.80665 m/s²                    = 3,138.13 m/s
delivered     = 14,352.58 × exp(−4,443.90 / 3,138.13)   = 3,482.78 kg
```

The anchors, the 320 s Isp, the 5% margin and the 150 m/s allowance come from aster: `src/v2/porkchop/launch-vehicles.ts`, and the live `estimate_mission_cost` (0.1.0) returns 3,482.7792 kg [Certain]. The payload-at-C3 curve already includes the injection burn, because the rocket's upper stage performs it. Charging it to the spacecraft as well gives 1,203 kg, 65% too low; `src/v2/SLICE_13_FOUNDING.md` DEC-13-4 calls this double count the slice's "#1 correctness hazard", and the budget type `SpacecraftDvBudget` has no injection field at all.

**11.** The runs are clustered, so 126 runs carry far less information than 126 independent trials (Sections B11.7.4 and B11.7.5):

```
cluster-bootstrap width = 45.60 − 6.09  = 39.5 points
Wilson width            = 31.95 − 17.22 = 14.7 points
ratio 2.68  →  design effect ≈ 2.68² ≈ 7.2  →  effective n ≈ 126 / 7.2 ≈ 17.5
```

Runs of one scenario are nearly all-or-nothing (four Sonnet scenarios scored 6/6 and fourteen scored 0), and the four shared-stimulus pairs are merged, leaving 18 clusters [Certain]. `clusterBootstrapCI()` in aster: `tools/slice16-harness/grade.mjs` resamples whole clusters 10,000 times with the mulberry32 generator and seed 20260727, and an independent re-implementation reproduces [6.09, 45.60] exactly. The data are worth about as many independent observations as there are clusters, so the wider clustered interval is the honest one. That is why the lock DEC-16-8 in `src/v2/SLICE_16_FOUNDING.md` replaced the draft's Wilson plan.

**12.** The release is already a fast periapsis, so the remaining kick is small (Sections C1.3 and C1.4):

```
v_rel at r_tip = 7,301 km:  7.5563 + 2.8 = 10.3563 km/s     (escape there: 10.4494 km/s)
kick from tether:  √(5 + 109.1905) − 10.3563             = 0.330 km/s
burn from LEO:     √(5 + 121.3210) − √(398,600 / 6,571)  = 3.451 km/s
injected mass (Isp 320 s, inert 0.15 kg per kg propellant):  4,427 kg  vs  1,165 kg
```

The release is only 93 m/s short of escape. By the Oberth effect a burn adds v·Δv + Δv²/2 of kinetic energy per kilogram, so a small Δv buys a lot of energy when you are already fast, and because the rocket equation is exponential, saving 3.12 km/s nearly quadruples the injected mass [Certain as arithmetic]. These figures reproduce PM-001, which exists only on the unmerged branch `origin/claude/skyhook-fixes-2026-10-22` (skyhook: `scripts/pm001_probe_analysis.py`). Its Isp and inert ratio are Conservative assumptions [Likely], and the 2.8 tier is a revenue-gated option, not the Rev A reference.

**13.** A fixed orbit plane limits the departure direction (Section C1.5):

```
DLA = asin( vz / |v∞| )        an orbit of inclination i contains only |DLA| ≤ i
equatorial tether: i = 0  →  only DLA = 0
deep-space fix:  |V − U| = √(v² + u² − 2uv·cos d),   d = max(0, |DLA| − i)
```

Release timing picks the asymptote's right ascension but cannot lift it out of the tether's plane, and skyhook: `params/rev_a.json` has no inclination field at all [Certain]. Only 13.3% of PM-001's 2,656 usable cells have |DLA| ≤ 5°, so most probes pay a deep-space correction burn; on the 2.8 tier the arrived-mass loss runs from 2.5% (1998 KY26) to 42.7% (Didymos), median 24.6% [Likely; recomputed for the guide from the unmerged PM-001 data] (Section C1.7). Aster grades only Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg (aster: `src/v2/core/lambert/feasibility.ts`): AMBER costs zero added Δv and RED gets a verdict, not a number. An equatorial "site" would have a 0° ceiling, so almost every cell would be RED and unpriced; a 28.5° orbit recovers much of the loss but drifts about 6.4° per day [Likely; J2 inputs from memory, verify].

**14.** 440.3996× is EQ-6 at 3.5 km/s, SF 2.5 and 0% derate, and skyhook: `finance/decision_grid.json` stores it correctly as `phase3_growth_option` / Optimistic [Certain]. In August it travelled without that label and was used for the 3.5 km/s tier, whose Conservative (30% derate) value is 3,085.95×; 3,085.95 / 440.40 = 7.007 is `handoff.md`'s "7× too light" (Section A11.17). Aster's envelope for 433 Eros (2032-06-10, 272 days, Falcon Heavy Expendable) cites eight sources, and `confidenceMin` in aster: `mcp/src/envelope/index.ts` takes the weakest, `cost-assumptions`, so the envelope says "assumed" while the `payloadAtC3` leaf stays "measured" [Certain, observed on 0.1.0] (Sections B10.6 and B10.8). "Assumed" says the 1,498.757 kg delivered mass rests on chosen modelling inputs (engine class, margin and allowance); it says nothing about accuracy, and only the leaf labels show which number is the weak link. Skyhook has no machine-enforced weakest-link rule, which is one thing Section C1.8 suggests it borrow.

**15.** Skyhook's CI ends by running `python3 physics/skyhook_physics.py`; with `v_orb_kms` set to 9.0 in a scratch copy, `verify_rev_a` prints a cross (16.04% error) and "FAILURES DETECTED", yet the `__main__` block never calls `sys.exit(1)`, so the script exits 0 and the step stays green [Certain, run for the guide] (Section A12.9). Only the earlier pytest step, through `test_rev_a_com_altitude`, would turn CI red. Aster's last recorded run (Slice 20 Front A, 2026-11-04) is 109/109 files and 360/360 tests, but 22 of those 109 test files do not use `node:test`, so each counts as one test however many checks it makes; a file with 200 checks reports `# tests 1` [Certain, demonstrated] (Section B8.11). The plain `npm test` glob reaches only 86 of the 109 files, and CI runs neither the MCP package tests nor the Slice 16 suite. In both repositories "green" means "these commands exited 0", not "every number was checked".

# Glossary

Every technical term the guide uses, with a short meaning and the chapters that explain it, first-explained chapter first. Project numbers in the meanings come from those chapters, which cite their repository sources.

| Term | Meaning | Explained in |
|---|---|---|
| \$k / \$M / \$B | Thousands, millions and billions of dollars. | A1 |
| 1.3 × V_c guardrail | The founding-document rule never to design above about 1.3 times the material's V_c 'at our required safety factor' without sign-off; Skyhook's tools read it in different ways (test: material V_c; site: working V_c with a 1.35 red line). | A6 |
| 1/sqrt(N) law | Sampling error shrinks with the square root of the number of draws, so halving it needs four times as many. | A8 |
| 68-95-99.7 rule | For a normal variable, about 68.27%, 95.45% and 99.73% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean. | A8 |
| `__main__` guard | The line `if __name__ == '__main__':`, which runs code only when a file is executed directly, not when it is imported. | A12 |
| Absolute error | The plain size of the difference between actual and expected values. | A12; also B8 |
| Absolute liability | Liability that applies without any need to prove fault. | A10 |
| Absolute magnitude (H) | A brightness scale for asteroids on which larger values mean fainter, hence usually smaller, bodies. | B1; also B4 |
| Absolute path | A path that starts from the top of the disk. | A12 |
| Absolute step tolerance | Stop when the change in x is smaller than a fixed amount in x's units. | B8 |
| AC-001 | Skyhook's anchor-customer ranking. | A10; also C1 |
| Acceleration | The rate at which velocity changes, in m/s². | A1; also A2 |
| Accelerometer | A sensor (essentially a mass on a spring) that measures non-gravitational forces per unit mass. | A2 |
| Accounting identity | The run-tests.mjs check that files discovered equals ok plus failed plus load-timeout files. | B12 |
| Accuracy | How close a number is to the truth. | A1; also B1 |
| Actuarial record | A history of outcomes that lets insurers price a risk. | A10 |
| Additive blending | Adding a drawn pixel's light to what is already on screen, so overlaps glow brighter. | B9 |
| Additive-only | A document rule where wrong lines are kept and corrections are appended as dated amendments. | B8; also B11 |
| Additive-only guard | The pre-commit check that blocks any deleted line in INVARIANTS.md, SLICE\_\*\_FOUNDING.md, src/v2/\*\_FOUNDING.md and src/v2/\*\_LOCKED.md files. | B12 |
| Aerothermal loads | The heating and pressure on a vehicle caused by moving through air. | A2 |
| `AGENTS.md` | Aster's rulebook for the people and AI agents working in the repository (roles, STOP gates, verify-before-lock, what a documentation agent may run); it names Hudson as final authority. | B1; also B5, B8, B9, B12 |
| AI agent | A language model that can call tools and then write an answer from their results. | B11 |
| Airspeed | Speed measured against the surrounding air, which turns with the Earth. | A4 |
| Albedo | The fraction of sunlight a surface reflects; Aster assumes 0.14 by default. | B1; also B11 |
| Aleatory uncertainty | True trial-to-trial randomness that more study cannot remove, such as navigation scatter on one approach. | A8 |
| `ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE` | The GPU driver's reported minimum and maximum drawable point size. | B9 |
| alpha | The opacity of a drawn pixel, from fully transparent to fully opaque. | B9 |
| Altitude | Height above Earth's surface; orbital radius equals Earth radius plus altitude. | A3 |
| Amendment (AMD) | A numbered, dated change appended to a locked decision or a pre-registration, quoting the old and new wording rather than overwriting them. | B1; also B10, B11, B12 |
| Amor | An NEA with a &gt; 1 AU and 1.017 &lt; q &lt; 1.3 AU, approaching Earth's orbit from outside without crossing (from memory, verify). | B3 |
| Amortization | Spreading a one-time cost over periods or units. | A9 |
| Ampere (A) | The SI unit of current, one coulomb per second. | A5 |
| Amplification factor | κ = (\|a\|+\|b\|)/\|a−b\|, the factor by which subtraction magnifies the inputs' relative error. | B8 |
| Anchor (camera) | The focused body the camera circles; the live landing view subtracts its position before rounding to float32. | B9 |
| Anchor (launch-vehicle curve) | One published (C3, payload) point on a vehicle curve, carrying its source and an 'official' basis. | B7 |
| Anchor customer | A first committed customer big enough to justify the build; the 2.8 km/s tier is gated on one. | A1; also A10 |
| Angular margin (marginDeg) | In the MCP output, how many degrees a cell's \|DLA\| sits inside (+) or outside (−) its active band edge. | B7 |
| Angular momentum | The amount of rotation an object carries about a point; at an apsis it is r times v and stays constant along a coasting orbit. | A3; also A5, A7 |
| Angular velocity (ω, angular rate, spin rate) | How fast an angle changes, in rad/s, equal to 2π divided by the time for one turn; for the tether ω = v_tip/L = 0.0078125 rad/s in Rev A. | A1; also A2, A3, A5 |
| Anomaly | An astronomers' term for an angle that locates a body on its orbit. | B3 |
| Anomaly tail | The 208 comets that arrive inside SBDB's neo group alongside the asteroids. | B4 |
| Apex touch | A passive catch that latches within tens of milliseconds of the instant of best velocity match (unmerged branch). | A8 |
| Aphelion distance (Q) | The farthest an orbit goes from the Sun, a(1 + e). | B3; also B4 |
| API | The set of names and functions a library offers to your code. | A12 |
| Apoapsis | The farthest point of an orbit from the central body (apogee for Earth, aphelion for the Sun). | A3 |
| Apogee | The highest point of an orbit. | A1; also A3, A4, A5, A10 |
| Apollo | An NEA with a &gt; 1 AU and q &lt; 1.017 AU, mostly outside Earth's orbit but crossing it (from memory, verify). | B3 |
| Apparent size | How many pixels an object spans on screen, set by its radius divided by its distance. | B9 |
| Append-only | A record where entries are only ever added, never edited or deleted; corrections are new entries. | A11 |
| Apsis (apsides) | Either the perigee or apogee, where the velocity is exactly perpendicular to the line to the centre. | A3 |
| Aramid | The Kevlar fibre family (from memory, verify), a low-creep reference class; HMPE creeps 3–5 times more (MP-001). | A6 |
| Arcsecond | 1/3600 of a degree. | B2 |
| Argument / return value | The inputs a function receives and the output it gives back. | A12 |
| Argument of perihelion (ω) | The angle within the orbit plane from the ascending node to perihelion, in the direction of motion. | B3 |
| Arithmetic mean | The sum of two numbers divided by two, the ordinary midpoint. | A11 |
| Arm (primary / control) | A branch of the experiment: the primary arm attaches the tools, the control arm asks the same questions with no tools. | B11 |
| Array (JSON) | An ordered list in square brackets, indexed from 0. | A1; also A11, A12 |
| Arrival v-infinity (v∞,arr) | The probe's speed relative to the target on arrival, which a rendezvous must cancel with the probe's own propellant. | B6; also B7, C1 |
| `as_of` | An envelope field giving the effective date of the data behind an answer; Aster sets it only where a launch vehicle is involved (2024-02-29). | B1; also B10 |
| Ascending node | The point where the body climbs up through the reference plane. | B3 |
| Ascent-loss ladder | The repo's Conservative/Baseline/Optimistic loss allowances of 1,800/1,500/1,200 m/s. | A4 |
| ASDS (Falcon 9 drone-ship recovery) | Falcon 9 flown with first-stage recovery on a drone ship at sea (autonomous spaceport drone ship; expansion from memory, verify), one of Aster's launch-vehicle configurations. | C1 |
| Assertion | A statement assert condition that makes a test fail if the condition is false. | A12; also B8, B12 |
| Assumptions | An envelope's list of plain-language modelling choices that the value depends on. | B10 |
| `aster-mission-mcp` | Aster's MCP server package on npm; 0.1.0, published 2026-07-10 and baked from commit 84fefe8 in a dirty worktree, is the only release. | B1; also B6, B10 |
| ASTM | A standards body whose published test methods labs follow (from memory, verify). | A6 |
| Astrometry | Measuring a moving object's position on the sky (two angles) at a known time. | B4 |
| Astronomical unit (AU) | The defined solar-system length 149,597,870,700 m, roughly the mean Earth–Sun distance. | B1; also B3 |
| Asymptote | The straight line the escape hyperbola approaches far from Earth, pointing along v∞,dep. | B7 |
| Aten | An NEA with a &lt; 1 AU and Q &gt; 0.983 AU, mostly inside Earth's orbit but crossing it (from memory, verify). | B3 |
| Atira / IEO | An NEA whose orbit lies wholly inside Earth's: a &lt; 1 AU and Q &lt; 0.983 AU (from memory, verify). | B3 |
| Atomic oxygen (AO) | Single, highly reactive oxygen atoms in low orbit that erode organic materials swept into them at orbital speed. | A6 |
| Atomic write | A file update that happens completely or not at all, done in Skyhook by writing a .tmp file and then calling os.replace. | A11; also A12 |
| Attribute | A shader input that differs for each point, such as position or size. | B9 |
| Audit | An organised search for defects by someone other than the author. | B8; also B12 |
| Audit-F2 | The Slice 18 finding that izzo lambert() mislabels a NaN position or a zero or infinite TOF as no_convergence, named to avoid collision with two other 'F2' findings. | B5 |
| AUP (assumption/uncertainty preservation) | Passes when stated confidence does not exceed the envelope's, every assumption string is acknowledged, and the prose neither overclaims nor denies assumptions. | B11 |
| Author | The identity git was configured with when a commit was made, which need not be the person or agent who typed the change. | B12 |
| Auxiliary circle | A circle of radius a centred on the ellipse's centre, used to define the eccentric anomaly. | B3 |
| Avalanche effect | The property that a one-byte change in input scrambles the whole digest. | A11 |
| Average cost | Total cost divided by units, which falls toward marginal cost as volume grows. | A9 |
| Axial stiffness (EA) | Young's modulus times cross-section area, measuring how hard a section resists stretching along its length. | A7 |
| Axis | One input dimension that varies across a grid. | A11 |
| Azimuth corridor | The set of launch azimuths a site may fly, e.g. 35–120° at Cape Canaveral. | B7 |
| B_min / practical window | The breadth qualifier of 2 departure cells; a window at least that wide is practical. | B6 |
| Baked provenance | A build-time file (baked-provenance.json) recording the commit, bake time and dirty flag, used when git is unavailable after an npx install. | B10 |
| Ballistic coefficient | Mass per unit of frontal area; a low value makes an object slow down high in the atmosphere. | A10 |
| Barycentric | Having its origin at the centre of mass of a group of bodies. | B2 |
| Base unit | One of the seven SI units defined on their own, such as the metre, kilogram and second. | A1; also A2, B1 |
| Base64 | A way of writing any bytes using only letters, digits, + and /. | B9 |
| bash | The standard Linux/macOS command shell that runs .sh files. | A12 |
| Basis value (A-basis, B-basis) | A materials-testing strength that a stated share of the population exceeds with stated confidence: a B-basis value is exceeded by 90% with 95% confidence, an A-basis value by 99% (from memory, verify); Skyhook's 'B01/95' label mixes the two and is never defined. | A6; also A8, A10 |
| Bay | The 40 km stretch of tether between two neighbouring nodes (SH-001 usage). | A7 |
| BCa | The bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap, a corrected interval method the harness does not use. | B11 |
| Bell curve (Gaussian) | A curve of the form e^(−constant × r²), flat-topped at the centre and falling away faster and faster; the shape of the tether's area profile and of the normal distribution's density. | A6 |
| Bernoulli trial | A single trial with two outcomes, success with probability p and failure with probability 1 - p. | A8; also B11 |
| Bessel's correction | Dividing a sample's squared deviations by n - 1 instead of n to avoid underestimating the spread. | A8 |
| Best practical window | The practical window with the lowest minimum C3, or an explicit no-practical-window state if none exists. | B6 |
| BF-001 | Skyhook's break-even frontier tool (tools/sims/skyhook_frontier.html): a decision plane of rocket-leg cost against the LEO launch-price floor, with the zero-margin contour drawn. | A1; also A10, C1 |
| Bias | A consistent offset in one direction that a small standard deviation does not reveal. | A8 |
| `bin` | The package.json field mapping a command name to the file that npx runs. | B10 |
| Binary file | A file whose bytes are meant for a program rather than a person, such as .xlsx or .pdf. | A11; also A12 |
| Binomial distribution | The distribution of the number of successes in N independent Bernoulli trials, with mean Np. | A8; also B11 |
| Birthday approximation | The estimate P ≈ 1 − exp(−n(n−1)/(2·16^k)) for the chance that two of n ids share their first k hex digits. | B12 |
| Bisection | Repeatedly halving a bracket that contains a yes/no flip until the flip point is pinned down. | A8; also A9 |
| Bit | A single 0 or 1. | A11; also A12, B8, B9 |
| Bit-identical | Two computations that produce exactly the same 64-bit floating-point numbers, not just close ones. | B5 |
| Blob | A chunk of bytes in browser memory that can be handed to the user as a downloaded file. | A12 |
| Body | The actual bytes carried by a response, such as a file's contents. | B9 |
| Boolean | A value that is either true or false. | A11 |
| Bootstrap (phasing strategy) | A phasing strategy where each phase is financeable alone, earns revenue or retires risk, and becomes part of the next. | A1 |
| Bootstrap (statistics) | Estimating sampling variability by resampling the data with replacement many times and recomputing the statistic. | B11 |
| Bottom-to-bottom interval | The time between successive passes of the lower tip through straight down, 2 pi/(omega - n), about 15.56 min for a rigid Rev A tether. | A2; also A3 |
| Bound orbit | An orbit with negative energy, a circle or ellipse that keeps returning. | A3 |
| Boundary layer | The code under src/v2/boundary/ that reads outside data and converts its units once on the way into the core. | B2 |
| Boundary-value problem (BVP) | A problem that gives conditions at both ends (start point, end point, duration) and asks for the starting velocity. | B5 |
| Bounded distribution | A distribution that cannot produce values outside fixed limits, as a triangle cannot. | A8 |
| Box-Muller transform | A recipe that turns two uniform random numbers into two independent standard normal numbers; the program site's g() keeps one. | A8 |
| Bracket | A pair of values chosen to bound an unknown, not an estimate of it. | A10 |
| Braid (12-strand single braid) | A rope made by interlacing strands; ST-001's test line interlaces 12. | A6 |
| Branch | A separate line of history in a repo; main is the official one, and an unmerged branch holds work not yet accepted into main. | A1; also A11, A12, B1, B12 |
| Branch (Lambert: left and right) | The two M ≥ 1 roots on either side of the T(x) minimum; the names refer to position relative to the minimum, not the sign of x. | B5; also B6 |
| Branch deploy | Serving a folder of a repository branch directly as a website. | B9 |
| `breadthCells` / `breadthDays` | A window's width in departure columns, and its derived day span (breadthCells - 1) times the departure step. | B6 |
| Break-even | The value of an input (price, volume, launch cost) that makes an outcome exactly zero. | A9; also C1 |
| Break-even price (p\*) | Price per kg at the catch at which a customer pays the same per arrived kg as with a dedicated rocket: (P_rocket/m_arr_rocket)\*(m_arr_skyhook/m_catch). | C1 |
| Break-even reuse factor (r\*) | The reuse factor at which the leg's per-flight cost exactly equals the ask, 0.527 for the 5 t Conservative case. | A4; also A10 |
| Breaking length | The longest uniform rope that could hang from its top in a steady 1 g field before breaking, σ/(ρg); about 379 km for Zylon. | A6 |
| Brotli | A stronger web compression format than gzip; offered by the browser but not returned by GitHub Pages. | B9 |
| Browser app | Aster's web pages: static files served by GitHub Pages from docs/, with all math running in the visitor's browser. | B1 |
| Budget class | A planning cost range for a phase, not a quote. | A1 |
| Build | The step that turns TypeScript sources into the bundled JavaScript a browser loads; Vite writes it into docs/. | B1 |
| Bundle | A built JavaScript file whose name carries a content hash. | B12 |
| Bundler | A build tool that gathers a program and its libraries into files a browser can load. | A12; also B9 |
| Burnout mass (mf) | Mass left when the propellant is gone: payload plus structure. | A1; also A4 |
| Bury | The length of tail tucked inside a hollow braid in a splice, which grips by friction and tightens under load. | A6 |
| Byte | Eight bits, a whole number from 0 to 255; files are sequences of bytes. | A11; also A12, B9 |
| C3 (characteristic energy) | Twice the specific orbital energy, v² − 2μ/r, in km²/s²; when positive it equals v∞², the square of the departure excess speed, and negative means still bound to Earth; the launch-energy currency of both projects. | A1; also A3, A4, A5, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B10, C1 |
| CA-001 | The unmerged canon claim audit (claude/creative-canon-claim-audit), a linter (canon/audit.py) that checks quoted numbers against rev_a.json through a registry of claim specs. | A11 |
| Cache | A store of previously downloaded files that the browser can reuse without downloading again. | B9 |
| Cached value (spreadsheet) | The last computed result of a formula saved in the file; absent for all 81 Design Calcs formulas in the Skyhook workbook. | A11; also A12 |
| Caching | Storing a derived value instead of recomputing it, which creates a copy that can go stale. | A11 |
| CAD (Close-Approach Data) API | JPL's Close-Approach Data service, which lists bodies passing within a given distance of a planet between two dates; it drives Gate 1 and the fidelity tiers. | B3; also B4 |
| Cadence | How often catches happen, in catches per day. | A1; also A9 |
| Camera | In Three.js, the viewpoint from which the scene is drawn. | B9 |
| Camera damping | Moving a camera a fixed fraction 1 - exp(-k dt) of the way to its target each frame. | A12 |
| Camera-relative rendering (floating origin) | Subtracting the camera position in f64 before converting to f32 so the GPU never holds huge absolute coordinates. | B1; also B9 |
| Canon | The official values, held in params/rev_a.json, Skyhook's single source of truth that all code must match. | A1; also A3, A5, A11, C1 |
| Canon drift | The gradual separation of quoted numbers from the canonical values. | A11 |
| Canon snapshot | A JSON copy of canon values embedded in a single-file tool and checked by exact-equality tests (unmerged fixes branch). | A11; also A12 |
| Canon test | A test comparing computed physics with stored rev_a.json values (6 of the 27 in test_rev_a_physics.py). | A12 |
| Canvas 2D | A browser drawing surface controlled by line and shape commands. | A12 |
| Capacity | The most the system can deliver per year (payload x cadence x 365). | A10; also C1 |
| Capex (capital expenditure) | Capital expenditure: money spent to build long-lived assets, mostly before they earn anything. | A1; also A8, A9 |
| Capex spread | How total capex is split across construction years (15/30/35/20% over years 1 to 4). | A9 |
| Capstan effect (Euler–Eytelwein equation) | Friction round a post multiplies grip exponentially with wrap angle, T_load/T_hold = e^(μθ), which lets dowel wraps grip a slippery line. | A6 |
| Capture envelope | The region a latch can accept; plus or minus 10 m in the founding document and site tool. | A8 |
| Carbon fibre | Fibre made of graphite-like carbon sheets, very stiff and strong but brittle (Toray T1000G, T1100G). | A6 |
| Carry | The time a caught payload rides the tether from the bottom to the top of the swing, about 466.8 s rigid at Rev A (476.3 s measured in the unmerged simulation). | A3; also A5 |
| Carry-aware model (M2) | The unmerged branch's TetherSim-validated model of the release state, which follows the centre of mass during the carry and gives a 32.4 m/s energy-equivalent deficit for Rev A. | A5 |
| Catastrophic cancellation | Loss of correct digits when subtracting two nearly equal large floating-point numbers. | B2; also B5, B8 |
| Catch | Latching a payload at the lower tip, ideally at zero relative speed; TetherSim models it as adding mass to the tip node. | A1; also A5 |
| Catch speed | The ground-relative speed the vehicle must match at the lower tip, v_orb − v_tip − 0.465 km/s = 4.59 km/s at Rev A. | A4 |
| Catch transient | The ringing of tether tension right after a payload is grabbed. | A7 |
| Caveat | A warning carried with data about how it may and may not be used. | A11 |
| CCSDS | The Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems, which sets common data formats (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| CDN | Public servers that host libraries so pages can load them by URL; offline, the page cannot. | A12; also B9 |
| Celestial equator | Earth's equator projected outward onto the sky. | B2 |
| Cell (agent study) | One scenario run on one model. | B11 |
| Cell (porkchop grid) | One (departure date, time of flight) pair on a porkchop grid. | B6; also B10, C1 |
| Cell (spreadsheet) | One box in a spreadsheet, holding a typed value or a formula. | A11; also A12 |
| Cell status | Each grid cell is ok (a branch converged), no_solution (the solver returned nothing) or stall (the solver returned branches but none converged). | B6 |
| Center code | The Horizons string (such as @sun, @ssb, 500@399) that states which body a file's vectors are measured from. | B2 |
| Central force | A force, like gravity toward Earth's centre, that always points at one fixed point, so it conserves angular momentum about that point. | A5 |
| Central limit theorem | The result that sums of many small independent effects, none dominant, tend toward a normal distribution. | A8 |
| Centre of mass (CoM) | The mass-weighted average position of a body or system, Σmᵢrᵢ/Σmᵢ; the skyhook spins about it while it orbits. | A1; also A2, A3, A7, B2, C1 |
| Centrifugal force | The apparent outward push felt in a rotating frame; it is a fictitious force. | A2 |
| Centripetal acceleration | The inward acceleration v²/r = ω²r needed to move on a circle; in orbit gravity supplies it, at a tether tip the tension does. | A1; also A2, A3, B3 |
| [Certain] | The confidence label for a textbook fact or a fact checked in the repository; Skyhook's own rule describes it as derivable from first principles or strong flight data. | A1; also A4, A11, B1, C1 |
| Character encoding | A table mapping byte values to characters, such as ASCII or UTF-8. | A11 |
| Characteristic velocity (V_c) | √(2σ/ρ), a fibre's built-in speed scale (an untapered tether with no payload can just reach it at SF 1); 2.73 km/s for Zylon in Rev A. | A1; also A2, A6 |
| Charge | The property of electrons and protons that makes them push or pull on each other, measured in coulombs. | A5 |
| Child process | A program started by another program, which holds both ends of the child's pipes; this is how an MCP host runs Aster's server. | B10 |
| Chord (c) | The straight-line distance between the start and end positions. | B5 |
| Chunk | One output file produced by the bundler. | B9 |
| CI (continuous integration) | A service that runs automated checks (tests, builds) on a fresh machine whenever code is pushed; a green check is not proof of correctness. | A1; also A2, A4, A7, A11, A12, B1, B9, B12, C1 |
| CI-vs-threshold reading | Calling a difference shown, ruled out or unresolved by comparing its interval with the pre-set threshold. | B11 |
| Circle | A conic with eccentricity 0, where the distance from the centre is constant. | B3 |
| Circular orbit speed (v_orb, EQ-2) | v = sqrt(mu/r), the speed needed for a circular orbit at radius r, computed by v_orbital_kms(); v_orb is its value at the tether CoM, about 7.556 km/s on the code's 6,981 km basis. | A1; also A3 |
| Cislunar | The region of space between Earth and the Moon. | A3; also A4, A10 |
| Claim | A sentence that says something is true, such as "the conservative tether weighs 609.1 t". | A11 |
| `clamp()` | A CSS function that picks a preferred size but keeps it between a minimum and a maximum. | B9 |
| Clamping | Pinning a value to the nearest end of an allowed range, as the 3D view does with time outside coverage. | B2 |
| Class | A blueprint for making objects that bundle named data together. | A12 |
| Classic script | A &lt;script src&gt; file that puts its names in one global space, e.g. THREE. | A12 |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The instruction file that briefs Claude Code sessions in the Skyhook repository: its five rules, open audit flags and the key equations EQ-1 to EQ-6. | A1; also A3, A4, A5, A6, A8, A9, A11, A12, B12, C1 |
| Clean-room implementation | Code written from a specification or paper without copying another implementation. | B5 |
| Client | A program that sends requests and receives responses: the browser asking a web server for files, or, in MCP, the part of the host that speaks MCP to one server. | B9; also B10 |
| Climb energy | The potential energy per kg needed to rise from the catch radius to the release radius, mu\*(1/r_low - 1/r_up); 5.25 MJ/kg for Rev A. | A5 |
| Climb penalty | The extra \~0.54 km/s an ideal vehicle needs beyond the catch speed to coast up to the 290 km tip (own analysis). | A4 |
| Clome | A name in Aster's process records that gates visual checks ('[V] visual (Hudson + Clome)') and may open primary sources under the two-run rule; AGENTS.md never defines it, and STATUS.md suggests a browser-automation agent [Likely]. | B1; also B12 |
| Clone / shallow clone | A downloaded copy of a repository with its history; a shallow clone holds only recent commits, so older commits are invisible locally though they still exist upstream. Skyhook's local clones hold the latest 50 of main's 59 commits; Aster's holds 175, back to 2026-09-21. | A1; also A11, A12, B10, B12 |
| Clopper-Pearson interval | An exact binomial interval; for 0 of 6 its upper bound is 45.9%. | B11 |
| Closed-world (openWorldHint false) | A tool that consults only its own committed data and never the internet. | B10 |
| CLPS | NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services program, which pays companies for lunar deliveries (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Cluster bootstrap | A bootstrap that resamples whole clusters, never single runs, so within-cluster likeness is kept. | B11 |
| Clustering | Trials grouped so that members of one group resemble each other, such as runs of one scenario. | B11 |
| CM-001 | Skyhook's draft conjunction white paper in docs/regulatory/, which proposes publishing the tips' shell-crossing times ahead; the committed file is a ZIP with a .pdf name. | A10 |
| CNT yarn | Yarn spun from carbon nanotubes, with lab strengths of 20–60 GPa that Skyhook has not re-verified. | A6 |
| Co-orbital | Aster's tag for Earth-like orbits: e &lt;= 0.1, i &lt;= 5 degrees and \|a - 1 AU\| &lt;= 0.05 AU (130 bodies). | B3; also B4, B6 |
| Coefficient of variation (CoV) | Standard deviation divided by the mean, a measure of relative scatter; ST-001 flags CoV above about 15%. | A6; also A8 |
| Coherent world | Frontier points where leg cost is 1-4 times the launch floor, a Speculative heuristic that both prices come from the same industry. | A10 |
| Collision (hash) | Two different inputs that produce the same hash digest. | A11 |
| Collision (mechanics) | A brief, strong interaction between bodies, in which momentum is always conserved. | A5 |
| Commit | A saved snapshot of every file in a repository, with message, author, time and parent commit(s), named by a hash such as 34935cb. | A1; also A11, A12, B1, B10, B12 |
| Commit hash (short hash) | A commit's fingerprint, 40 hex characters for git's SHA-1; citations use the short hash, its first 7 hex characters, e.g. 34935cb. | A12; also B10, B11, B12 |
| Commit message | The text describing a commit; Aster requires the form type(scope): description. | B12 |
| Common cause | A shared driver that makes several risks move together and so creates correlation. | A8 |
| Compiler | A tool that turns one form of code (e.g. JSX) into another the browser can run. | A12 |
| Complement (economics) | A good that helps your business, as cheap construction launch lowers Skyhook's capex. | A10 |
| Complement (probability) | The event that A does not happen, with probability 1 - P(A). | A8 |
| Component (user interface) | A function that takes inputs (props) and returns a piece of user interface, in React (Skyhook tools) or Preact (Aster). | A12; also B9 |
| Components (of a vector) | The parts of a vector along chosen perpendicular axes, for example (v_x, v_y). | A2; also B2 |
| Composite grid | A grid that takes, cell by cell, the lower-C3 answer of the M=0 and M=1 grids and records which family won. | B6 |
| Composition of rotations | Applying rotations one after another, where order matters, as the Keplerian propagator does (orbit plane to ecliptic, then ecliptic to equatorial). | B2 |
| Composition rule | A published formula a consumer applies itself, such as delivered_plus_leg = leg + delivered. | A9; also A11 |
| Compounding | Interest earning interest, which makes growth follow (1 + r) to the power t. | A9 |
| Compression (data) | Rewriting a file into fewer bytes by replacing repeated patterns with short references. | B1; also B9 |
| Compression (mechanical load) | A pushing load; a tether can carry tension but not compression. | A1 |
| Compression ratio | Decoded bytes divided by wire bytes. | B9 |
| Computed signal | A signal derived from other signals that recalculates only when one of its inputs changes. | B9 |
| Concave | Curving downward, so that the average output is at most the output at the average input; NPV is concave in the derate. | A8 |
| Condition code U | The MPC's integer 0–9 rating of orbit uncertainty: a logarithmic band of along-orbit runoff with base about 4.42. | B4 |
| Confidence class | Aster's three-level label (measured, derived, assumed) saying how a number was obtained. | B1; also B4, B10, C1 |
| Confidence interval | A range built by a procedure that captures the true value in a stated share (usually 95%) of repeats; it covers sampling noise only. | A8; also B11 |
| Confidence label | A tag ([Certain], [Likely], [Speculative]) stating how strong the evidence is for a claim. | A1; also A8, A11 |
| Confound | A second difference between conditions that could explain a result instead of the factor being studied. | B11 |
| Conic equation | r = p / (1 + e cos nu), which gives the Sun distance at any true anomaly for every conic. | B3 |
| Conic sections | The four curves (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) that a plane cuts from a cone, and the only shapes a two-body orbit can take. | B3 |
| Conjunction | A predicted close approach between two objects in orbit. | A10 |
| Conjunction management | Avoiding collisions between the tether and other objects in orbit. | A1 |
| Connected component / 8-connectivity | A maximal group of member cells linked through neighbours; under 8-connectivity, cells touching at an edge or a corner count as linked. | B6 |
| Conservation of angular momentum | With only a central pull, the quantity \|r x v\| stays constant, which is what Kepler's second law expresses. | B3 |
| Conservation of momentum | With no outside force, the total momentum of a group of objects never changes. | A4; also A5 |
| Conservatism ladder | Three columns of assumptions (Conservative, Baseline, Optimistic); the financial base case uses Conservative only. | A1; also A8, A9, A11 |
| Conserved quantity | A quantity that never changes while a closed system runs on its own. | A7; also B8 |
| Constant | A variable the code promises not to change, written in capitals by convention. | A12 |
| Constellation | A fleet of many satellites working together, such as Starlink or OneWeb. | A10 |
| Construction launch price | The \$/kg paid to launch the tether's own material while building it. | A1; also A9 |
| Consuming boundary | The place in the code where a vector's numbers are actually used, such as the DLA computation. | B2 |
| Content hashing | Putting a file's fingerprint into its name so that new content always gets a new URL. | B9 |
| Contour | A line joining points of equal value on a chart: equal C3 on a porkchop plot, or zero margin (the break-even line) on a decision plane. | A10; also B6 |
| Contrast | A comparison between two conditions that is planned in advance. | B11 |
| Contrast ratio | A measure from 1:1 to 21:1 of how readable text is against its background. | B9 |
| Contribution margin | Price minus variable cost per unit, the amount each unit contributes toward fixed costs. | A9; also A10 |
| Converged | No longer changing as the model is refined to more nodes. | A7 |
| Convergence | The property that successive iterates approach the true answer. | B8 |
| Convex | Curving upward, so that the average output is at least the output at the average input. | A8; also B7 |
| Coordinate system | An origin plus three perpendicular axes plus a unit. | B2 |
| Coordinates | The numbers a frame assigns to a point. | B2 |
| Copyright | Legal protection of a program's expression, not of the mathematics it implements (general principle, not legal advice). | B5 |
| `core.hooksPath` | A local git setting naming the folder git looks in for hooks; without it git ignores .githooks/. | B12 |
| Coriolis force | A fictitious sideways force that acts in a rotating frame on objects moving within that frame. | A2 |
| Correlation (ρ) | A number from -1 to +1 measuring how strongly two quantities move together along a straight line. | A8 |
| Cost | Money the business spends. | A9 |
| Cost-estimating relationship (CER) | A rule predicting cost from size, usually cost ∝ mass^b, with b below 1 meaning economies of scale. | A4; also A10 |
| Coulomb (C) | The SI unit of charge. | A5 |
| Counterfactual | A 'what if' run that changes one input to see how much it matters. | A10 |
| Covariance | The unscaled measure of how two quantities vary together, E[(X - muX)(Y - muY)]. | A8 |
| Covariance matrix | The table of element uncertainties and their correlations produced by the orbit fit. | B4 |
| Coverage (envelope field) | An envelope field stating how many results were returned out of how many, and by what selection rule. | B1; also B10 |
| Coverage (ephemeris) | The time span for which every loaded ephemeris series has data, the intersection of their ranges. | B2 |
| Creep | Slow permanent stretching of a fibre under a steady load. | A1; also A6, A9, A10 |
| Creep rate / creep life | Strain per unit time under sustained load, and the time to rupture, each stated at a given load fraction and temperature. | A6 |
| Creep rupture | Failure after a long time under sustained load at a stress well below the short-term strength. | A6 |
| CRLF | The two-byte line ending carriage return 0x0D plus line feed 0x0A used on Windows (from memory, verify). | A11; also A12, B4 |
| Cross product | a × b, a vector perpendicular to both inputs with length \|a\|\|b\| sin θ and direction set by the right-hand rule; ω × r gives a rotating point's velocity. | A2; also A5, B2, B5 |
| Cross-field check | A validation rule that compares fields, such as requiring the start date to come before the end date. | B10 |
| Cross-link | A secondary (diagonal) strand in a Hoytether that connects parallel primary lines and redistributes load around damage. | A6 |
| Cross-section / cross-sectional area | The face you would see if you cut a cable straight across, and the size of that face. | A6 |
| CSS | The language for a web page's look and layout. | A12; also B9 |
| CSS pixel | The unit of length that page layout uses. | B9 |
| Cubic Hermite interpolation | Fitting the cubic curve that matches positions and velocities at both bracketing samples, Aster's only core interpolator. | B2; also B8 |
| Cumulative cash flow | The running total of net cash flows up to a given year. | A9 |
| Cumulative distribution function (CDF) | F(x) = P(X &lt;= x), rising from 0 to 1. | A8 |
| Current (I) | The charge flowing past a point each second, measured in amperes. | A5 |
| Customer segment | A group of buyers with similar needs, such as GEO satellite operators or lunar-lander companies. | A10 |
| CUT RULE | A pre-declared order for dropping scope, with each cut recorded. | B1 |
| Cutover bar | The maximum interpolation error allowed for a body, set at 3 × the measured maximum rounded up (for example 0.5 km for Earth). | B2 |
| CW-001 | The unmerged catch-window study (docs/research/cw001_catch_window.md on claude/creative-catch-window-lab), which puts the passive velocity-match window at about 98 ms. | A2; also A8 |
| Damping | Any effect, like friction, that drains energy out of a vibration; undamped means there is none. | A7 |
| Damping ratio (ζ) | A dimensionless damping setting where 0 is none and 1 (critical) just stops a single spring-mass from oscillating; the model's per-segment value is nominal. | A7 |
| Data | Recorded values such as 610, "Zylon PBO" or 2026-07-02. | A11 |
| Data arc | The number of days between the first and last observations used in an orbit fit. | B4 |
| Dataclass | A Python record type that bundles named fields; frozen=True stops them being changed. | A11; also A12 |
| DEC (decision record) | A numbered decision in a slice's founding document, written DEC-&lt;slice&gt;-&lt;n&gt;, locked with its justification and never silently revised. | B1; also B8, B11, B12 |
| Deciles | The nine cut points that split sorted data into ten equal parts; sensitivity.py takes the first and ninth as P10 and P90. | A8 |
| Decision plane | A chart with two unknowns on its axes so that every point is a possible world. | A10 |
| `DECISION_LOG.md` | Skyhook's log of design decisions and corrections (docs/DECISION_LOG.md), such as lowering the reference tip speed from 3.5 to 2.8 to 2.5 km/s. | A1; also A3, A4, A6, A8, A9, A10, A11 |
| Declarative | A style of code that describes what the result should be and lets a library work out the steps. | B9 |
| Declination | The angle of a sky direction north (+) or south (−) of the celestial equator. | B7; also C1 |
| Declination ceiling (dlaCeilingDeg) | The largest \|DLA\| a site can reach directly: the maximum of min(i, 180° − i) over every inclination its corridor allows. | B7 |
| Decoded bytes | The size of a file after decompression, which sets parse time and memory. | B9 |
| Decomposition | Splitting a lump sum into parts, each with a documented source. | A9 |
| Dedicated launch | Buying a whole rocket for one customer. | A4 |
| Deep-space manoeuvre (DSM) | A probe correction burn far from Earth, \|V - U\| by the law of cosines, used in PM-001 to fix the direction an equatorial release cannot supply. | C1 |
| Degeneracy | A special case that is mathematically valid but physically meaningless, such as a near-zero-C3 close-approach cell. | B1; also B5, B6 |
| Delivered cost per kg | All costs divided by all kilograms delivered; Skyhook's model spreads capex straight-line over 15 mature years with no discounting. | A9 |
| Delivered mass | Launch-vehicle payload at the cell's C3 times exp(−Δv_sc/(g₀·Isp)); arrival wet mass, with no injection term. | B7 |
| Delta-v (Δv) | A change in velocity, supplied by a burn or a tether throw, in km/s; the currency in which every spaceflight manoeuvre is costed. | A1; also A3, A4, A10, B1, B7, C1 |
| Demand | What customers will actually buy per year. | A10; also C1 |
| Demise | Burning up on reentry. | A10 |
| Density | Mass per unit volume. | A1; also A6 |
| Departure date | The launch date of a candidate transfer; with the time of flight it fixes the transfer, and their sum gives the arrival date. | B6 |
| Deposit | Anything that raises the tether's orbit: a catch of descending mass, ED reboost or EP reboost. | A5 |
| Deprecated | Still working but marked for removal in a future version. | A7; also A12 |
| Depreciation | The accounting practice of spreading an asset's cost over its life on paper; absent from this cash model. | A9 |
| Derate | A planned cut in usable fibre strength for joints, seams and ageing; 30% in the conservative case. | A1; also A6, A9, A11 |
| Derate ladder | The three canon derate rungs, 0% (Optimistic), 15% (Baseline) and 30% (Conservative), that express conservatism in the mass model. | A6 |
| Derivative | The rate of change of one quantity with respect to another at an instant, such as dr/dt. | A2; also A7 |
| Derived unit | A unit built from base units, such as the newton or joule. | A1; also A2, B1 |
| Derived value | A value computed from inputs by a stated formula, such as V_c or the 121.83x mass ratio. | A11 |
| Design effect (DEFF) | The factor 1 + (m-1)rho by which clustering inflates variance compared with independent trials. | B11 |
| Design lock | The 2026-07-27 founding-document section 9 that froze the Slice 16 design as its first pre-registration. | B11 |
| Design revision | A frozen, named version of the design; Rev A is Skyhook's current one. | A1; also A11 |
| Design system | The full set of tokens and shared components an interface is built from. | B9 |
| Design token | A named value, such as a colour, used instead of a raw literal so meaning is defined once. | B9 |
| Designation | An object's official label: a number such as 433, or a provisional label such as 2026 GG. | B4 |
| Deterministic (deterministic model) | Always giving the same output for the same inputs; a deterministic model keeps all randomness in its inputs, and Aster's stricter sense is bit-identical outputs from the same inputs, code and environment. | A8; also B8 |
| Deterministic grading | Scoring by a fixed program using only string and number operations, so the same input always gets the same grade. | B11 |
| Deviation | A place in the Skyhook repository that knowingly uses a number different from canon and says so. | A11 |
| Deviations register | Skyhook's list (docs/DEVIATIONS.md) of places that knowingly show non-canonical numbers, each with a disposition. | A11 |
| Device pixel | A physical dot on the screen. | B9 |
| Device pixel ratio (DPR) | The number of device pixels per CSS pixel, often 2 on high-density screens. | B9 |
| Diameter formula | D(km) = (1329/√p)·10^(−H/5), which turns brightness into size only once an albedo p is assumed. | B4 |
| Dictionary (dict) | Python's mapping of keys to values, the equivalent of a JSON object. | A12 |
| Diff | The list of changed lines between two versions, computed when asked for. | B12 |
| Differential equation | An equation containing a derivative, giving a rule for how a quantity changes from its current value. | A7 |
| Diffing | Comparing the old and new virtual trees so only changed DOM nodes are updated. | B9 |
| Digest (hash) | The fixed-length output of a hash function. | A11; also A12 |
| Digital twin | A computer model detailed enough to stand in for the real machine in tests. | A1; also A2, A7, A12 |
| Dilution | An RMS or mean made smaller by adding easy zero-error points, although nothing improved. | B8 |
| Dimensional analysis | Checking that the units on both sides of an equation match. | A1 |
| Dipole field | A bar-magnet-like field, like Earth's far from the surface, whose strength falls as 1/r^3. | A5 |
| Directed acyclic graph (DAG) | A network of nodes joined by one-way arrows with no loops; in git each arrow points from a commit to an earlier one. | B12 |
| Direction | The way a vector points. | A2 |
| Dirty worktree | A working copy of the code holding changes that were never committed. | B1; also B10 |
| Disclosure unit is a date | Slice 18's rule that a body's limit is stated as the date its screening stops being supported, not as a distance. | B3 |
| Discount (frontier) | How far under the incumbent's price Skyhook is assumed to sell, 30% by default. | A10 |
| Discount factor | 1/(1 + r)^t, the multiplier that converts year-t money to today's money. | A9 |
| Discount rate | The yearly rate used to shrink future money to present value; 10% in the headline NPV. | A1; also A9 |
| Discounted payback | The first year the discounted cumulative cash turns positive; for a spend-first project at a positive rate, never earlier than plain payback. | A9 |
| Dispatch | One scoped instruction packet given to the executing agent. | B1; also B12 |
| `.dispatch-scope` | A plain-text allowlist of path patterns that a dispatch may commit, checked by the pre-commit hook. | B12 |
| Dispersion | The spread (sigma) of an error, as in the site's position, velocity and timing sliders. | A8 |
| Displacement | The change in position between two moments. | A2 |
| Display axis | A plotting axis that is not a model input; the grid's leg-cost axis is one. | A9; also A11 |
| Disposition | The single decided action recorded for a deviation or audit finding, such as fix, leave or label. | A11; also B12 |
| Distribution | The full description of how likely each value of a random variable is. | A8 |
| DLA (declination of the launch asymptote) | The angle north or south of Earth's equator of the departure excess-velocity direction, arcsin(v∞,z / \|v∞\|) in an equatorial frame. | B1; also B2, B7, B10, C1 |
| `dla_feasibility` | Aster MCP tool that returns the DLA and the launch-site verdicts for one cell. | B1; also B2, B5, B7, B10, C1 |
| Docstring | The explanatory text at the top of a Python function. | A1; also A2, A4, A11 |
| Does not close | A design state where MR·ε ≥ 1, so no rocket of any size can carry any payload. | A4 |
| Dogleg | A plane change made during ascent: the rocket flies an allowed azimuth and then turns. | B7; also B10 |
| DOI | A Digital Object Identifier: a permanent identifier for a published object. | B11 |
| DOM | The live tree of page elements that JavaScript can read and change. | A12; also B9 |
| Dot product | ax·bx + ay·by + az·bz = \|a\|\|b\|cos θ, a scalar that measures how much two vectors point the same way. | B2; also B5 |
| Double-count guard | DEC-13-4's rule that injection is never charged to the spacecraft, because payload-at-C3 already includes it. | B7 |
| Down-mass | Payloads coming down from higher orbits, whose catch would add energy to the tether. | A5 |
| Draft | A work-in-progress file kept on purpose but not authoritative, such as params/service_mxer_draft.json. | A11 |
| DRAFT / PROPOSED / RULED / LOCKED | The status words for a founding doc or decision: AI-drafted, awaiting Hudson, decided by Hudson, and approved so that only amendments may change it. | B12 |
