| Drag loss | Δv spent pushing through the air. | A4 |
| Drift (of a conserved quantity) | The relative change \|X(t) - X(0)\|/\|X(0)\| of a quantity that should be conserved. | A7 |
| Dual oracle | Validation that uses poliastro for bulk cells plus an independent float64 T(x) scan near the T_min boundary. | B5 |
| Duck typing | Recognising a kind of object by its fields alone; Aster treats any object with a numeric value and string units as a Quantity. | B10 |
| Duty factor | The fraction of time reboost thrust is usable, bracketed at 0.3-0.5 in finance/reboost_bound.py. | A5 |
| Dynamic load factor | The ratio of peak transient tension to steady tension during a catch, estimated at about 1.30–1.47 in Skyhook's models and labelled Speculative. | A2; also A6, A7 |
| Dynamic pressure | ½·rho·v², the effective wind pressure on a body moving through air. | A3 |
| Dynamics | The study of how a system changes over time under forces. | A7 |
| e (Euler's number) | The mathematical constant 2.71828…, the base of natural logarithms and the limit of (1 + 1/n)ⁿ. | A1; also A4, A6 |
| E-notation | The computer form of scientific notation, e.g. 3.986e14. | A1 |
| Eager loading | Downloading a file before first paint without the user asking. | B9 |
| Earth-centred inertial frame (ECI) | A non-rotating frame centred on Earth with axes fixed to the stars; the twin and the physics module work in it. | A2; also A7 |
| Earth-rotation credit (v_earth) | The 0.465 km/s eastward speed an equatorial launch pad already has, which EQ-3a subtracts from the catch speed; any eastward equatorial rocket gets it, so it is not a tether benefit. | A1; also A2, A4 |
| Eccentric anomaly (E) | A helper angle measured at the ellipse's centre, linked to time by Kepler's equation and to position by r = a(1 − e cos E). | B3 |
| Eccentricity | A number that measures how stretched an orbit is: 0 is a circle, near 1 a long thin ellipse, 1 a parabola, above 1 a hyperbola. | A3; also A5, B3 |
| Eccentricity band | Aster's four e ranges (A &lt; 0.1, B &lt; 0.2, C &lt; 0.3, D otherwise) assigned by eccentricityBandForBody. | B3; also B4 |
| Ecliptic | The plane of Earth's orbit around the Sun, seen from Earth as the Sun's yearly path among the stars. | B2 |
| Ecliptic frame | A coordinate frame whose z-axis points along the pole of Earth's orbit, about 23.4° from the equatorial pole. | B7 |
| Ecliptic pole | The direction perpendicular to the ecliptic plane, the +Z direction of ecliptic frames. | B2 |
| Ecological validity | How closely a test situation resembles real-world use. | B11 |
| Economies of scale | The effect, when the CER exponent is below 1, that twice the mass costs less than twice as much. | A10 |
| EDT | US Eastern Daylight Time, four hours behind UTC (the -0400 in commit dates). | A11 |
| Effect | Code that re-runs automatically when any signal it read changes. | B9 |
| Effective mature years | The sum of ramp multipliers over the operating years (9.9 for 11 Conservative years). | A9 |
| Effective modulus (E_eff) | The model's chosen Young's modulus, working stress divided by target strain (3.248e11 Pa). | A7 |
| Effective sample size | The number of independent observations the clustered data are worth, n/DEFF. | B11 |
| Effective tip mass | How heavy the tip of a free spinning rod feels to a sideways shove, 1/(1/M + L^2/I), about 82.9 t for Rev A. | A5 |
| Efficiency (η) | Useful output divided by input. | A5 |
| Eigenvalue calculation | A standard matrix method that finds the frequencies at which a whole mass-spring system can vibrate in step. | A7 |
| Elastic | Describes a material that returns to its starting length when the load is removed. | A6 |
| Elastic / inelastic demand | Demand is elastic when a price cut raises total revenue (E &lt; -1) and inelastic when it lowers it (-1 &lt; E &lt; 0). | A10 |
| Elastic collision | A collision in which kinetic energy is kept. | A5 |
| Electric propulsion (EP) | Thrusters that use electricity to accelerate propellant to very high exhaust speed. | A5 |
| Electrical power | P = V\*I, the energy per second a current delivers through a voltage. | A5 |
| Electrodynamic (ED) reboost | Restoring the tether's orbit by pushing a solar-powered current through it against Earth's magnetic field, without propellant. | A1; also A5, A9 |
| Electrodynamic (ED) tether | A long conductor in orbit used as a generator or motor against Earth's magnetic field. | A5; also A10 |
| Electron | Rocket Lab's small orbital launcher, the cost anchor in leg_cost.py at \$7.5M per flight. | A4 |
| Ellipse | A closed conic with eccentricity between 0 and 1, the shape of every bound orbit, with the central body at one focus. | A3; also B3 |
| elvperf | NASA Launch Services Program's interactive query tool for launch-vehicle performance; Aster's source for payload-versus-C3 data. | B7 |
| EMF (electromotive force) | A voltage source, despite the name. | A5 |
| Encounter δv | The velocity kick from a planetary flyby, estimated as 2v·sin(atan(μ/(d·v²))) and multiplied by the remaining time to test whether the encounter is material. | B4 |
| End-for-end splice (mid-line splice) | A splice that joins two pieces of line in line, the geometry a segmented tether needs; no controlled public data exist for it. | A6 |
| End-of-year convention | Treating each year's cash as arriving at the end of that year, so year 1 is discounted once. | A9 |
| Energy | The capacity to do work, measured in joules. | A3; also A5, A7 |
| Energy method | Finding the ideal Δv from the energy per kilogram an orbit needs, ignoring the path. | A4 |
| Energy per kilogram | What km²/s² measures (1 m²/s² = 1 J/kg); C3 is twice the orbit's energy per kilogram. | B1 |
| Energy-equivalent deficit | The cut in release speed at the canon release point that gives the same delivered energy as the real, finite-mass throw. | A5 |
| `engines.node` | The package.json field declaring the minimum supported Node.js version (&gt;=18 here, untested). | B10 |
| Environment variable | A named setting passed to a program by the shell that starts it, such as ASTER_PUSH_OK=1. | B12 |
| Ephemeris (plural ephemerides) | A table of where bodies are (and, in Aster, how fast they move) at listed times. | A10; also B1, B2, B9 |
| Epistemic limit | A limit on what the server knows, as opposed to a fact about the world; refusals are reserved for these. | B10 |
| Epistemic uncertainty | Uncertainty from lack of knowledge, which evidence such as a quote, test or customer would shrink. | A8 |
| Epoch | A reference instant at which a frame or quantity is frozen or measured. | B2; also B3, B4 |
| EQ-1 to EQ-7 | Skyhook's numbered physics equations: EQ-1 rocket equation, EQ-2 circular speed, EQ-3 tip speeds, EQ-4 characteristic velocity, EQ-5 taper, EQ-6 tether mass ratio, EQ-7 release energy. | A1; also A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A9, A10, A11, C1 |
| EQ-3 | The repo's first-order tip-kinematics equations: upper tip v_orb + v_tip, lower tip v_orb - v_tip (- 0.465 ground-relative), tip acceleration v_tip^2/L. | A2 |
| EQ-7 | The repo's upper-tip release equation: energy at r_tip = 7,301 km gives C3 and apogee, implemented in apogee_from_release(); named only in the physics module docstring. | A3 |
| Equatorial frame | A coordinate frame whose z-axis points along Earth's rotation pole; ICRF is aligned with it. | B2; also B7 |
| Equatorial prograde | An orbit in the equatorial plane moving in the same direction Earth turns. | A4 |
| Equatorial radius | Earth's radius at the equator, about 6,378 km (from memory, verify); the basis of rev_a's stored com_radius_km 6988. | A1; also A3, A11 |
| Equatorial-plane loss | Arrived mass lost because the tether releases only in the equator plane, versus an unconstrained departure (2.5-42.7%, median 24.6%, in Chapter C1's reconstruction; PM-001's own text says 3-43%). | C1 |
| Error code −32602 | The JSON-RPC "Invalid params" code, which this SDK puts inside the text of an isError tool result rather than in a JSON-RPC error object. | B10 |
| Error function (erf) | erf(x) = (2/√π)∫₀ˣ e^(−t²) dt, the scaled area under a bell curve, rising from 0 toward 1; appears in EQ-6 (0.9857 at the Rev A x). | A6; also A7, A8, A12 |
| ES module | A JavaScript file that uses import and export, loaded with type='module'. | A12 |
| esbuild | The fast transpiler Vite uses to strip TypeScript types (0.21.5 in package-lock.json). | B9 |
| Escape hyperbola | The open orbit followed after the injection burn, which never returns to Earth. | B7 |
| Escape speed (escape velocity) | The smallest speed at which an object never falls back, √(2μ/r), which is √2 times circular speed at the same radius. | A3; also B6 |
| `estimate_mission_cost` | Aster MCP tool that runs the delivered-mass screening chain for one cell and launch vehicle; despite its name it returns kilograms, not dollars. | B1; also B5, B7, B10, B11, C1 |
| Estimation | Measuring a quantity and reporting how uncertain the measurement is, rather than a yes/no test. | B11 |
| Eval | A structured measurement of a model's behaviour on fixed tasks. | B11 |
| Eval pair | A question paired with a fixed tool call and a deterministic JavaScript check over the result. | B10 |
| Event | A group of outcomes you care about, such as 'latched'. | A8 |
| Event loop | The browser mechanism that feeds the main thread one task at a time. | B9 |
| Evidence | Whatever lets a reader check a claim without trusting its author: an equation, a source, a passing test or a re-runnable file. | A11 |
| Evidence envelope | The JSON wrapper every MCP tool returns, carrying value, confidence, provenance, assumptions, validity range and optional refusal. | B1; also B10, B11, C1 |
| Evidence system | The set of files and habits that keeps a project's claims checkable over time. | A11 |
| Evidence-carrying decision | One tool envelope that an answer relies on, which is the unit each dimension is graded on. | B11 |
| Executable assertion | Code that checks an invariant and fails loudly when it breaks. | B8 |
| Exhaust | The hot gas a rocket throws backward to push itself forward. | A4 |
| Exhaust velocity (v_e) | The speed of a rocket's exhaust relative to the rocket, v_e = Isp × g₀, used in the rocket equation. | A1; also A4, A5, B7 |
| Exit code | The whole number a program returns when it ends; 0 means success, and CI steps pass or fail on it. | A11; also A12, B12 |
| Expected loss | Probability of loss times value lost. | A10 |
| Experiment | Anything with an uncertain result, such as one catch attempt. | A8 |
| `explain_cell` | Aster MCP tool that returns the derivation trail for one departure/time-of-flight cell. | B1; also B5, B6, B10, B11 |
| Explicit Euler | The simplest integrator, which steps using only the slope at the start of the step and gains energy on undamped oscillators. | A7 |
| Exploratory analysis | A result labelled as outside a study's official output, so it can suggest but not confirm; the guide labels its own Slice 16 model contrast this way because the repository never computed it. | B11 |
| Exponential function (exp) | The function eˣ, written exp(x), whose slope everywhere equals its own value; it describes growth at a rate proportional to size. | A1; also A4, A6 |
| Exponential growth | Growth by the same multiplying factor in each equal step, rather than the same amount. | A4 |
| Exposure | Likelihood times impact, an ordinal score from 1 to 25. | A10 |
| Extrapolation | Extending a result beyond the modelled range by assuming a pattern continues. | A9; also B2, B7, B10 |
| Eye splice | A loop made by tucking a line's end back into itself, retaining about 90% of the line's strength in HMPE (LR-001). | A6 |
| FAA/AST | The US FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation, which licenses launch and reentry (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Fail-closed / fail-open | Fail-closed means refusing or reporting failure when unsure rather than returning a possibly wrong answer; fail-open means silently allowing. | B5; also B11, B12 |
| Failure vs error (pytest) | A failure is a false assertion or a crash in the test body; an error is a crash in setup (a fixture) before the test body runs. | A12 |
| Faithful transmission | An answer that keeps the envelope's numbers, refusals, sources and uncertainty intact. | B11 |
| Fallback default | A hardcoded value a program uses when real data is missing; it keeps tools running on stale numbers. | A11 |
| False precision | Printing more significant figures than the inputs justify, such as Aster's 16–17-digit radii and C3 values from 2–4-figure inputs. | B1; also B4 |
| Fast-forward | A merge where the target branch label simply slides forward because nothing diverged. | A12; also B12 |
| Fault-based liability | Liability that applies only if the party is shown to be at fault. | A10 |
| FCC | The Federal Communications Commission, which licenses radio spectrum and in 2022 adopted a 5-year post-mission disposal rule for LEO (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| `fetch-depth: 0` | A checkout setting that downloads full git history instead of one commit. | B12 |
| Fibre | A very thin, very long strand whose molecules are aligned along its length, which makes it strong in tension. | A6 |
| Fictitious force | An apparent force that appears only because the observer's frame is accelerating or rotating. | A2 |
| Fidelity tier | Aster's per-body label L0, L1 or L2 for how far its two-body screening can be trusted for that body. | B1; also B3, B4, B10, C1 |
| Field of view (FOV) | The angle a camera sees from the top to the bottom of the image. | B9 |
| Figure of merit | The single number that ranks materials for a given job. | A6 |
| File | A named sequence of bytes stored on a disk. | A12; also B9 |
| File mode 100755 / 100644 | Git's record of a regular file that is executable (755) or not (644); git ignores a non-executable hook. | B12 |
| `file://` vs `http://` | Opening a file directly versus through a web server; ES modules and fetch need http. | A12 |
| Files whitelist | The package.json list of the only paths packed into the published tarball. | B10 |
| Final-mass fraction | 1/MR, the share of lift-off mass left after the burn (payload plus structure). | A4 |
| Finite tether mass correction | The reduction in delivered C3 and apogee because a real tether slows when it throws a payload; canon assumes infinite mass. | A3 |
| First-class result | A result with the same standing and shape as any other, so an agent can branch on it. | B10 |
| Fixed block | In the frontier tool, the per-kg sum of insurance, facility amortization, ops and reboost electricity (\$550/\$385/\$241). | A10 |
| Fixed cost | A cost that does not change with volume sold, such as Skyhook's \$80M/yr fixed ops. | A9; also A10 |
| Fixed reference budget | The single 1000 + 150 + 50 m/s spacecraft budget that the compare page applies to every body when computing delivered mass. | B6 |
| Fixed-step | Using the same time step for the whole run. | A7 |
| Fixed-timestep accumulator (Gaffer loop) | A render loop that banks real frame time and spends it in fixed physics steps so physics never depends on frame rate. | A7; also A12 |
| Fixture (pytest) | A set-up function whose result several tests share. | A7; also A12 |
| Fixture (test data) | A committed data file of inputs, sometimes with expected outputs, that tests (and in Aster the app) read and replay. | B1; also B5, B8 |
| Fixture scope | How long a fixture's result is reused: per function, class or module. | A12 |
| Flaw | A tiny crack, void or chain defect at which a fibre breaks first, like the weakest link of a chain. | A6 |
| Flexible (dynamics) | Allowing the parts of a model to stretch and bend rather than staying rigid. | A7 |
| Flight heritage | Hardware or physics that has already flown. | A10 |
| Flight-path angle (γ) | The angle between the direction of travel and the local horizontal. | A4 |
| float32 (single precision, f32) | The 32-bit float format GPUs use, with 24 significant bits (about 7 decimal digits) and epsilon 2⁻²³ ≈ 1.19e-7. | B8; also B9 |
| float64 (double, f64) | A 64-bit floating-point number (53 significant bits, about 16 decimal digits); every JavaScript number and every Aster core quantity is one. | B2; also B8, B9 |
| Floating-point number | A number stored as a fixed count of significant binary digits times a power of two; a 64-bit double keeps about 15–17 significant digits, so some decimals such as 1/60 are inexact. | A11; also A12, B1, B8, B9 |
| FNV-1a | A simple, fast non-cryptographic hash used for the 64-bit prompt-prefix fingerprint; good for spotting accidental change, not tampering. | B11 |
| Focus | One of the two fixed points that define an ellipse; the central body (Earth for Skyhook, the Sun for Aster) sits at one focus of every orbit. | A3; also B3 |
| Folded normal | The distribution of the size \|T\| of a normal error ignoring its sign; P(\|T\| &lt;= w) = erf(w/(sigma\*sqrt 2)). | A8 |
| Folder (directory) | A container that holds files and other folders. | A12 |
| Force | A push or pull, measured in newtons, where 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². | A3; also A5, A6 |
| Formula cell (spreadsheet) | A cell expression such as =B3\*2 that computes a value from other cells. | A11; also A12 |
| Founding document | A slice's written contract, using a §1–§8 template, normally committed before any implementation. | B1; also B11, B12 |
| Fraction | Here, a ratio between 0 and 1, such as derate_fraction 0.3. | A1 |
| Fragment shader | A shader that runs once per covered pixel and sets its colour and alpha. | B9 |
| Frame (render) | One redraw of the picture on screen. | A12 |
| Frame budget | The time available to prepare one frame, 1000 ms divided by the refresh rate. | B9 |

| Frequency (f) | The number of laps per second, f = 1/T. | A2 |
| (from memory, verify) | The guide's marker for a fact recalled rather than read in a repository file, which should be checked before use. | A1; also B1, Front matter |
| Front | A sub-track of work inside a slice. | B1; also B12 |
| Frozen dataclass | A dataclass whose fields cannot be changed after creation, like ScenarioInputs. | A12 |
| Frozen-centre closed form (M1) | The scale estimate 2\*m\*v_tip/(M+m), which assumes the system centre of mass does not move during the carry; in M1 it is both the tether's speed loss and the payload's release shortfall (30.7 m/s for Rev A with a 200 t hub). | A5 |
| FULL faithfulness | The logical AND of every applicable dimension for a run. | B11 |
| Function | A named reusable recipe that takes arguments and returns a value. | A12 |
| Future value (FV) | What a present amount grows to at a given interest rate. | A9 |
| G&A | General and administrative cost, the overhead of running the organisation. | A9 |
| G-load | An acceleration expressed as a multiple of g0, n = a/g0. | A2 |
| Gantt chart | A bar chart of tasks against time. | A1 |
| Garden of forking paths | The bias that comes from making analysis choices after seeing the data, which tends to favour flattering results. | B11 |
| Gate | A yes/no check that must pass before something is accepted: in Skyhook an automated test, in Aster's Slice 18 one of three tests a body must pass. | A7; also B4 |
| Gauss hypergeometric function | The special function ₂F₁(a, b; c; z), used here as a series (hyp2f1b) to compute T(x) accurately near the parabola. | B5 |
| Gaussian copula | A technique that keeps each input's own distribution shape but correlates the draws through linked normal numbers. | A8 |
| Gel spinning | Drawing polyethylene fibre from a gel so its very long chains line up almost perfectly. | A6 |
| Generated output | A file written by a program rather than by hand, which must be regenerated when its inputs change. | A11 |
| Generator (drag) mode | An ED tether letting its own EMF drive current, which makes electricity and lowers the orbit. | A5; also A10 |
| GEO (geostationary orbit) | Geostationary orbit, a circular orbit 35,786 km up where a satellite circles once per day. | A1; also A3, A5, A10 |
| Geocentric | Having its origin at the centre of the Earth. | B2 |
| Geometric albedo (p_V) | The fraction of visible light a surface reflects back toward the source, relative to an ideal flat white disk of the same size. | B4 |
| Geometric distribution | The distribution of the number of attempts until the first success, with mean 1/p. | A8 |
| Geometric mean | The square root of the product of two numbers, the midpoint on a log scale. | A11 |
| `get_body` | Aster MCP tool that returns one body's full record, or the refusal not_found. | B1; also B3, B8, B9, B10, B11 |
| `get_validation_report` | Aster MCP tool that reads the committed solver-validation results. | B1; also B5, B8, B10, B11, B12 |
| Gigapascal (GPa) | One billion pascals, which equals 1,000 newtons per square millimetre. | A6 |
| Git | A version-control tool that records every change to the files. | A1; also A12, B1, B10, B12 |
| `git diff` | The command that shows line-by-line changes between two versions. | A12 |
| `git diff --numstat` | A git output giving added and deleted line counts per file, which the hook uses to count deletions. | B12 |
| Git hook | A script git runs automatically at a fixed moment, such as before a commit or push; Aster uses hooks to enforce dispatch scope and block pushes. | B1; also B12 |
| `.gitattributes` | A git settings file kept in the repository that can fix line-ending handling for everyone; Skyhook's main has none. | A11; also A12 |
| GitHub Actions | GitHub's CI service, configured by workflow files in .github/workflows/. | A12; also B12 |
| GitHub Pages | GitHub's static web hosting, which serves files committed to a repository (for Aster, its docs/ folder). | A12; also B9 |
| `.gitignore` | A list of file patterns git must never record, such as Python and pytest caches. | A12 |
| glob | A filename pattern in which \* stands for any run of characters; in a filename glob \* does not cross /. | B12 |
| GNC | Guidance, navigation and control. | A10 |
| Golden file (golden reference) | A stored reference output from a trusted run that later runs or other implementations must reproduce, such as tools/twin/golden.json. | A7; also A11, A12 |
| Golden number (pinned value) | A stored output that the code must keep reproducing exactly; a golden-numbers test pins it so any silent change fails. | A12; also B8, B12 |
| Governance | The part of process that says who may decide what. | B12 |
| GPU | The graphics processing unit, a processor that colours many pixels in parallel and works in 32-bit floats. | A12; also B1, B9 |
| Grapple | The catching mechanism at the tether tip. | A1; also A2 |
| Grapple terminal authority | How far the tip's grapple can reach on its own; the site code subtracts it from the position miss. | A8 |
| Gravitational parameter (μ, GM) | The gravitational constant times a body's mass: 3.986 × 10¹⁴ m³/s² (398,600 km³/s²) for Earth in rev_a.json; Aster uses the Sun's value for heliocentric orbits. | A1; also A3, A4, A5, B3, B5 |
| Gravitational potential energy | Energy stored by position in a gravity field, -mu·m/r, negative because zero is set at infinite distance. | A3; also A5, B3 |

| Grep | A command-line tool that searches text across files. | A4; also B1 |
| Grid (decision grid, lookup table) | The model evaluated at many input values and saved for lookup by another program. | A9; also A11 |
| Gridded ion thruster | An electric thruster that accelerates ions through charged grids. | A5 |
| Gross mass (m0) | Total lift-off mass: payload plus structure plus propellant. | A1; also A4 |
| Ground-relative speed | Speed measured against Earth's spinning surface. | A1; also A2, A4 |
| GTO (geostationary transfer orbit) | Geostationary transfer orbit, a long ellipse whose high point reaches toward GEO altitude. | A1; also A3, A4, A5, A10, C1 |

| (guide-computed) | The guide's marker for a value produced for this guide by running the repository's own code read-only, without changing any file. | A7; also A3 |
| gzip | The common web compression format, which the host applies to Aster's files. | B9 |
| Half-length (L) | Distance from the centre of mass to one tip; 320 km in Rev A. | A1; also A2 |
| Hall-effect thruster | An electric thruster that accelerates ions with crossed electric and magnetic fields; named with gridded ion thrusters in the founding doc as the reboost backup. | A5 |

| Hardware mass factor | The workbook multiplier (1.8/1.6/1.4) on tether launch cost that stands in for the hub, arrays and tips. | A5; also A9 |
| Harness | The program in tools/slice16-harness/ that sends each scenario to a model, executes its tool calls against the MCP server and records everything. | B11 |
| Hash function (hash) | A function that turns any bytes into a short fixed-length fingerprint (digest) that changes completely if any byte changes; git names commits this way. | A9; also A11, A12, B1, B4, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 |
| Hashing basis | The exact bytes a recorded hash was computed over; STATUS.md named it as the OQ-17-7 blocker because a CRLF checkout hashes differently, a gap the .gitattributes eol=lf setting has since closed. | B4 |
| HASTE | Rocket Lab's suborbital Electron variant (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron), with no published \$/kg. | A4 |
| HASTOL | Hypersonic Airplane Space Tether Orbital Launch, a Boeing / Tethers Unlimited tether-launch study (\~1999–2001); the glossary's 'closest literature ancestor'. | A1; also A2, A3, A4 |
| HEAD | The commit the working files were checked out from. | B10; also B12 |
| Headers | Labelled metadata in a request or response, such as the content encoding. | B9 |
| Headless Chrome | Chrome run without a window, driven by a program; used for twin QA and to print the teaser HTML to PDF. | A12 |
| Headroom | Gap between break-even price and Skyhook's own delivered cost (BF-001: rocket-leg cost plus fixed block, on a 2.5-tier basis). | C1 |
| Held-out points | Test points the model never used, such as the elvperf queries at C3 = 15, 25, 35 and 50. | B7; also B8 |
| Heliocentric | Having its origin at the centre of the Sun. | B2 |
| Hexadecimal | Base-16 notation using digits 0-9 and a-f, used to write bytes and hashes compactly. | A11; also A12 |
| High-elliptical orbit | A strongly stretched ellipse with a high apogee, such as the Rev A throw with e = 0.852. | A3 |
| Historical record / current-state record | An append-only log of the past versus a file that must be refreshed from commands to stay true, such as STATUS.md. | B12 |
| HMPE (UHMWPE) | High-modulus polyethylene fibre (Dyneema, Spectra), the core fibre of Rev A's construction baseline (naming from memory, verify). | A1; also A6, A10 |
| Holm correction | A step-down procedure that tests sorted p-values against alpha/(m-i+1) to control false alarms across several contrasts. | B11 |
| Honest mode / readable mode | Honest mode shows real sizes and distances; readable mode may enlarge bodies but must keep provenance and honesty labels. | B1 |
| Honest rounding | A quote whose distance from the true value is at most half the place value of its last written digit. | A11 |
| Honesty layer | The enforced rules that make every number show its unit, source and trust level and make the software refuse rather than guess. | B1; also B9, B10 |
| Hook (React / Preact) | A function such as useState or useEffect that gives a user-interface component memory or side effects between redraws. | A12; also B9 |
| Hooke's law | The rule that a spring's force is proportional to its stretch. | A7 |
| Host (MCP) | The AI application a person uses, such as a chat app or coding agent; it holds the MCP client, and with the stdio transport it launches the server as a child process. | B10 |
| Householder's method | A root finder that also uses the third derivative; Aster's Lambert iteration, converging with order 4 (from memory, verify). | B5; also B8 |
| Hoytether | A tether of many parallel load-bearing lines joined by cross-links, so a cut line's load moves to its neighbours; mandatory for all Skyhook flight tethers. | A6 |
| HTML | The language for a web page's structure. | A12; also B9 |
| HTTP request | A message from the client asking a server for a resource at a path. | B9 |
| HTTP response | The server's reply, made of a status code, headers and a body. | B9 |
| HTTP status code | The number a web server answers with: 200-299 mean OK, 400 bad request, 404 not found and 429 too many requests (a quota block). | A12; also B9, B11 |
| Hub | The central station of the tether, carrying power, control and ballast. | A2; also A3, A5, A10 |
| HUD (heads-up display) | The text panel drawn over a 3D view: tip speed, tension and energy drift in Skyhook's twin; date and coverage in Aster's scene. | A7; also A12, B2, B9 |
| Hudson, Nova, Codex, Claude Code | The owner with final authority, the advisor who drafts, the code executor, and the docs/recon agent that also executes when Codex is unavailable. | B1; also B12 |
| Hurdle rate | The minimum return an investor will accept. | A9 |
| Hybrid D=200 partition | Aster's drawing-only spatial grid of 1 AU cubes, with any cube holding more than 200 bodies split into 0.25 AU sub-cubes. | B4 |
| Hydrolysis | A reaction with water that cuts polymer chains, sped up by heat. | A6 |
| Hyperbola (hyperbolic trajectory) | An open conic with eccentricity above 1: the path of a body with positive orbital energy, which escapes with speed to spare. | A3; also B3, B6 |
| Hyperbolic excess speed (v∞, v-infinity) | The speed left over relative to a planet once its gravity no longer matters, √C3 at departure; in the patched-conic model, the difference between the spacecraft's and the planet's heliocentric velocities. | A3; also B1, B5, B6, B7, C1 |
| Hypersonic | Faster than about five times the speed of sound (from memory, verify). | A1; also A4 |
| Hypothesis | A testable prediction, such as one model's rate being at least 10 points above another's. | B11 |
| Hysteresis | Using different thresholds for entering and leaving a state so a value near one threshold does not flicker. | B9 |
| H–G system and slope parameter G | A model of how an asteroid brightens toward zero phase angle, with the slope parameter G setting the steepness; G is null for every body in Aster. | B4 |
| Ideal rendezvous | The model's assumption that the payload arrives with exactly the tip's velocity (zero relative velocity). | A7 |
| Idempotent | A property of an operation where calling it twice has the same effect as calling it once. | B10 |
| IEEE 754 | The international standard for floating-point arithmetic; its 64-bit double-precision format is float64. | A12; also B8 |
| Ill-conditioned | A problem in which tiny input errors cause large changes in the answer. | B5 |
| Impact (I) | A 1-5 score for how bad a risk's consequence is. | A10 |
| Impact parameter | The distance by which a body's straight incoming path would miss the planet's centre; Aster's flyby formula uses closest-approach distance and speed instead. | B4 |
| Imperative | A style of code that says step by step what to do. | B9 |
| Import | Loading another module so its names can be used. | A12 |
| Import graph | The network of files reached by following every import from a starting file. | B9 |
| Import map | A JSON block telling the browser what a bare module name like 'three' points to. | A12; also B9 |
| Import-time loading | Work done when a module is first imported, such as skyhook_physics.py reading rev_a.json into PARAMS. | A12 |
| `importorskip` | A pytest call that skips a test or whole file if a library is missing. | A12 |
| Impulse | Average force times the time it acts (J = F\*dt), equal to the change in momentum, measured in N\*s. | A5 |
| In-orbit cover | Insurance on an asset in orbit, charged per year. | A10 |
| In-space fork | A draft, non-canonical variant that catches a payload from circular LEO and throws it onto a GTO-class transfer. | A5; also A9, A10 |
| Inclination | The tilt of an orbit's plane against a reference plane, 0° to 180°: Earth's equator for Earth orbits, the ecliptic for Aster's asteroid elements; rev_a.json has no inclination field. | A3; also A4, A5, B3, B7, C1 |
| Independence | Two events or quantities are independent if knowing one tells you nothing about the other, which lets their joint probability be found by multiplying; both of Skyhook's Monte Carlos assume it. | A8 |
| Inelastic collision | A collision in which some kinetic energy turns into heat, sound or vibration. | A5 |
| Inertia | The tendency of an object to keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless a net force acts on it. | A2 |
| Inertial frame | A frame that neither accelerates nor rotates relative to the distant stars, in which Newton's laws hold as written. | A2; also A3, A7, B2 |
| Inertial speed | Speed measured in a frame centred on Earth that does not rotate (fixed against the distant stars). | A1; also A4, A5 |
| Infeasibility as a value | Convention DEC-15-4(g): a known negative answer such as {feasible: false, reason} is returned as a value with normal provenance, not as a refusal. | B10 |
| Infinite-tether-mass limit | The assumption, built into canon release values, that the tether is so heavy it does not notice the payload it throws. | A3; also A5 |
| Infinity | A special floating-point value produced by results such as 1/0. | B8 |
| Infrastructure | The machinery, such as hooks and CI servers, that runs a project's checks. | B12 |
| Initial-value problem (IVP) | A problem that gives the starting position and velocity and asks where the object ends up. | B5 |
| Initialize | The first MCP message, in which client and server agree a protocol version and exchange names, versions and capabilities. | B10 |
| Injected mass | Mass that stays on the departure trajectory after the kick stage's propellant and inert mass are gone. | C1 |
| Injection (injection burn) | The burn that turns circular parking-orbit speed into the hyperbola needed for a given C3, dv = sqrt(C3 + 2mu/r_p) - sqrt(mu/r_p). | B6; also B7 |
| Inlining | Writing a very small file directly into the JavaScript as text instead of shipping it separately. | B9 |
| Input | A value someone chose or measured, such as 610 km altitude or 5.8 GPa strength. | A11 |
| Input hardening | Making a function reject invalid inputs (unknown mode, NaN, infinite or negative values) with an error instead of computing a number. | B7 |
| Insurance | Transfer of a risk to an insurer in exchange for a payment. | A10; also C1 |
| Insured value | What the insurer pays on a total loss. | A10 |
| Integer | A whole number, stored in Python as type int. | A11 |
| Integral | A sum of very many very thin slices, used here to add up the load or mass along an arm. | A6 |
| Integrator | A method that turns the current rate of change into the state one time step later. | A7 |
| Inter-catch interval | The time between catches, 365.25 days divided by catches per year. | A5 |
| Interaction | When two inputs moved together change the output by more or less than the sum of their separate effects. | A8 |
| Internal rate of return (IRR) | The discount rate at which NPV equals zero; Skyhook's finance code does not compute it. | A9 |
| International Celestial Reference Frame (ICRF) | The modern realisation of equatorial axes, tied to distant quasars and within about 17 mas of the J2000 mean equator. | B2; also C1 |
| Interpolation | Estimating a value between known points, such as stored ephemeris samples or grid points; in the twin it also means blending two physics states for smooth drawing. | A7; also A9, A11, A12, B1, B2, B10 |
| Interpolation fidelity | How far an interpolated value can be from the true model value; the grid's worst case is 0.0611%. | A11 |
| Interpreter | The program (python3) that runs Python code top to bottom. | A12 |
| Intraclass correlation (ICC) | How alike runs in the same cluster are, from 0 (no more alike than random) to 1 (identical). | B11 |
| INV-004 | Aster's invariant that a frame round trip must return the input within 10 × Number.EPSILON relative error, applied to heliocentric-scale inputs. | B2 |
| INV-014 | An Aster invariant ID that carried two meanings until ruling R2 namespaced them: INV-014a is the 8.5 star-background floor and INV-014b the three-gate visualization-tier contract. | B12 |
| INV-015 | Aster's invariant that the Lambert solver must trace to a peer-reviewed algorithm; its text still names Izzo 2014 via PyKEP source compiled to WebAssembly, which Revision 2 replaced without the amendment INV-015 requires of itself. | B5 |
| INV-021 | Aster's rule that the frame of any quantity derived from Lambert vector components must be established by numerical measurement at the consuming boundary, never from a label. | B2 |
| INV-024 | Aster's rule that outside astrodynamics libraries serve as validation oracles only: their code is never imported, ported or transcribed into the math layer. | B1; also B5 |
| INV-032 | Aster's rule that no non-finite number (NaN or Infinity) may cross the wire, because JSON.stringify silently turns them into null; the envelope builder enforces it. | B1; also B10 |
| INV-S16-035 | The Slice 16 local invariant that reported rates are the ones in the founding document at lock, with exploratory observations labelled exploratory in a separate section. | B11 |
| Invariant (INV) | A numbered technical rule that must hold at all times so tests and reviews can check it. | B1; also B2, B4, B8, B11, B12, C1 |
| Inverse CDF | The function that answers 'which value has a share u of the distribution below it?'. | A8 |
| Inverse-square law | A quantity that falls as 1/r², so doubling the distance cuts it to one quarter. | A3 |
| Inverse-transform sampling | Producing draws from any distribution by feeding uniform random numbers into its inverse CDF. | A8 |
| Ionosphere | The thin layer of charged gas (plasma) around Earth that closes an ED tether's circuit. | A5 |
| ITAR / EAR | International Traffic in Arms Regulations and Export Administration Regulations, the US export-control rules for defence and dual-use technology. | A10 |
| Iteration | Solving an equation by starting from a guess and repeatedly improving it. | B8 |
| Iteration cap | A maximum number of iterations after which the method reports failure. | B8 |
| Izzo's x variable | A single variable that sweeps every conic joining two points: −1&lt;x&lt;1 ellipse, x=1 parabola, x&gt;1 hyperbola, with a = s/(2(1−x²)). | B5 |
| I²R loss | Heat lost in a wire, which grows with the square of the current. | A5 |
| J-curve | The dip-then-rise shape of cumulative cash for a project that spends before it earns. | A9 |
| J2 (oblateness effect) | The effect of Earth's equatorial bulge, which slowly turns orbit planes; Skyhook's repository does not model it. | A3; also C1 |
| J2000 | Aster's time anchor, JD 2451545.0, noon on 2000-01-01. | B1; also B2 |
| J2000 ecliptic | The frame Aster stores elements in: the plane of Earth's orbit frozen at J2000, with zero longitude at the vernal equinox. | B3 |
| JavaScript (JS) | The programming language web browsers run. | A7; also A12, B9 |
| Jekyll | A site generator GitHub Pages runs by default, disabled for Aster by an empty .nojekyll file. | B9 |
| Jensen's inequality | For a convex function g, E[g(X)] &gt;= g(E[X]) (reversed for concave); plugging in average inputs does not give the average output. | A8 |
| Job (CI) | One independently run unit of a CI workflow, made of steps. | B12 |
| Joint efficiency (η) | Breaking force of a joined line divided by that of the plain parent line; Rev A requires at least 85%. | A6 |
| Joule (J) | The SI unit of energy, N·m. | A1; also A5 |
| JPL Horizons | NASA/JPL's ephemeris service, the source of every Aster planet and moon state-vector file. | B2; also B3, B4 |
| JSON | A plain-text format for structured data made of objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true/false and null. | A1; also A11, A12, B1, B9, B10, B11 |
| JSON Schema | The language-neutral standard for writing schemas as JSON; the MCP SDK publishes draft-07 schemas in tools/list. | B10 |
| JSON-RPC 2.0 | A small protocol for remote function calls in which requests and responses are JSON objects matched by a numeric id. | B10 |
| JSX | JavaScript with HTML-like tags mixed in, used by the React web library. | A1; also A12 |
| Julian Date (JD) | A continuous count of days in which each day starts at noon, so .5 marks a midnight. | B1; also B2, B10, C1 |
| K1 return leg | Slice 20's asteroid-to-Earth Lambert grid that exports Earth-arrival v-infinity as a vector with its epoch. | B12; also C1 |
| K2 (idea kernel) | An Aster strategy idea that builds on K1 and asks whether an inbound payload's Earth-arrival v∞ fits Skyhook's catch envelope. | C1 |
| Kapton | A polyimide film used as the standard reference material in atomic-oxygen exposure tests (from memory, verify). | A6 |
| kB versus KiB | 1 kB is 1,000 bytes (SI) while 1 KiB is 1,024 bytes (binary). | B1 |
| Kepler's equation | M = E − e sin E, which links time (mean anomaly M) to position (eccentric anomaly E) on an ellipse and must be solved by iteration. | A3; also B3 |
| Kepler's first law | Bound orbits are ellipses with the central body at one focus. | A3; also B3 |
| Kepler's second law | A line from the central body to the orbiting body sweeps equal areas in equal times, so the body moves fastest at its closest point. | A3; also B3 |
| Kepler's third law | The square of an orbit's period is proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis. | A3; also B3 |
| Kerolox / methalox / hydrolox | Kerosene, methane or hydrogen burned with liquid oxygen, the main chemical propellant pairs. | A4 |
| Key (JSON) | A name in double quotes that labels a value. | A1; also A11 |
| Key (list item) | A stable identifier on a list item that lets the diff match old rows to new rows. | B9 |
| Key-value pair | A key followed by a colon and the value stored under it. | A11 |
| KeyError / undefined | What Python raises, and what JavaScript silently returns, when code reads a key that does not exist. | A1 |
| Kick | A burn by the payload's own engine or kick stage after release, to make up any shortfall to its target orbit or C3. | A3; also C1 |
| Kick stage | A small rocket a payload carries to add the final Δv after release or from a parking orbit. | A4; also A10, C1 |
| Kilonewton (kN) | One thousand newtons. | A2 |
| Kilowatt-hour (kWh) | One kilowatt for one hour, exactly 3.6 MJ of energy. | A1; also A4, A5, A9 |
| Kinetic energy | Energy of motion, ½·m·v². | A3; also A5, B3 |
| Kármán line | The conventional edge of space at 100 km altitude (from memory, verify). | A3 |
| L0 | The tier for bodies that do not exist or cannot be propagated (11 bodies). | B3; also B4 |
| L1 | The tier for bodies supported only until a dated material close approach (10,150 at 10^6 km against the 2026-09-11 CAD snapshot). | B3; also B4 |
| L1 support boundary | For a fidelity-tier-L1 body, the first material encounter date; cells or windows arriving on or after it rest on an orbit the encounter invalidates, which appears as a diagonal on the porkchop. | B6; also C1 |
| L2 | The tier for bodies whose error Aster cannot bound or has not measured (31,745). | B3; also B4 |
| Ladder conflation | The recorded error of encoding different destinations (tip speeds) in columns meant to vary only caution. | A9 |
| Lagrange's time-of-flight equation | The classical formula giving flight time from a, s and c through angles α and β, with case switches. | B5 |
| Lambert solver | Code that finds the orbit joining two given positions in a given flight time; Aster's follows Izzo 2014. | B1 |
| Lambert's problem | Finding the two-body orbit that joins two positions in a given flight time. | B4; also B5, C1 |
| Lambert's theorem | The classical result that flight time depends only on a, r1 + r2 and the chord c. | B5 |
| `lambert_unconvergeable` | The catalogue-cache status meaning no Lambert solve converged at any grid point for a body; defined end to end but never assigned. | B5 |
| Lane multiplier (lane multiple) | The frontier tool's price multiple over the launch price for a destination lane (GTO 2.2x, GEO 3.5x, cislunar 6.0x), an unvalidated internal assumption. | A9; also A10 |
| Latitude | The angle of a launch site north or south of Earth's equator. | B7 |
| Lattice (porkchop grid) | The regular grid of departure-date and time-of-flight sample points that Aster evaluates; each sample point is a cell. | B6 |
| Launch azimuth | The compass heading of the rocket's flight, measured from north; 90° is due east. | B7 |
| Launch cover | Insurance that protects the launch phase. | A10 |
| Launch period | The span of days, often weeks, during which a mission needs a launch opportunity every day. | B7 |
| Launch vehicle | The rocket that lifts the spacecraft from Earth and injects it onto its departure trajectory. | B7 |
| Launch window | The minutes within one day during which a launch can reach the required trajectory. | B7 |
| Launching state | A state that launches, procures the launch of, or provides the territory or facility for a launch (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Lazy import | Importing a library inside a function so the rest of the module works without it. | A12 |
| Lazy loading | Downloading a file only when it is needed. | B9 |
| Leaf | A value in a JSON tree that is not an object, such as a number or string. | A11; also B1 |
| Leap second | Extra seconds inserted into UTC now and then to keep clocks in step with Earth's rotation (from memory, verify). | B1; also B2 |
| Least squares | Choosing the orbit that minimises the sum of squared, noise-weighted differences between observed and computed positions. | B4 |
| Ledger | A JSON Lines file with one row per run, holding the prompt, every tool envelope, the reply and token usage. | B11 |
| Leg ask | The \$2,835/kg the project would like to pay for the rocket leg, half the Falcon 9 max-performance GTO premium. | A4 |
| Legend | The colour bar sampled on the same log path as the heatmap, with ticks 1, 10, 100, 1000 and the words 'logarithmic scale'. | B6 |
| LEO (low Earth orbit) | Low Earth orbit, a few hundred kilometres up (formally up to about 2,000 km; from memory, verify). | A1; also A3, A4, A5, A10, C1 |
| Letter of intent (LOI) | A non-binding statement of interest, weaker than a contract. | A10 |
| Level of detail (LOD) | Swapping cheaper drawings for objects that appear small on screen. | B9 |
| Levelized cost | In textbook finance, the present value of costs divided by the present value of output (the constant price that makes NPV zero); the model's delivered cost is not one. | A9 |
| LF (line feed) | The single byte 0x0A that ends a line on Linux and macOS (from memory, verify). | A11; also A12, B4, B9 |
| Liability Convention | The 1972 UN treaty setting absolute liability for damage on Earth or to aircraft and fault-based liability for damage in space (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Library | Reusable code written by someone else. | A12 |
| Libration | Pendulum-like swinging of a tether about the local vertical. | A7; also A10 |
| Likelihood (L) | A 1-5 score for how probable a risk is. | A10 |
| [Likely] | The confidence label for a claim supported by evidence but not proven; Skyhook's rule adds that it may rest on minor modelling assumptions. | A1; also A4, A11, B1, C1 |
| Line of nodes | The line where the orbit plane cuts the reference plane. | B3 |
| Linear colour scale | A colour mapping that gives equal colour steps to equal differences of the value. | B6 |
| Linear density (λ) | Mass per metre of cable, equal to density times solid area. | A6 |
| Linear growth | Growth by the same added amount in each equal step. | A4 |
| Linear interpolation (piecewise-linear) | Joining neighbouring samples with straight lines, segment by segment; Aster's founding rule forbids it in any core/ path, but the launch-vehicle curves in src/v2/porkchop/ use it between anchors. | B2; also B7 |
| Linear spacing | Axis values separated by equal added steps. | A11 |
| Linearise | Replace the full equations with their straight-line approximation for small wobbles about a steady motion. | A7 |
| Linter | A program that scans files for suspicious patterns, such as misquoted canon numbers. | A11 |
| List price | An advertised price, not one a customer is known to have paid. | A4 |
| `liveMin` | The lowest finite converged C3 anywhere on a body's live grid. | B6 |
| LLM judge | A second language model used to score answers, banned in Slice 16 by DEC-16-9. | B11 |
| LM-001 | The unmerged leg make-or-buy study (finance/LEG_MAKE_OR_BUY_FINDINGS.md on claude/creative-leg-make-or-buy), which finds nothing closes under Rule 4 at the \$2,835/kg leg ask once the sortie is costed. | A4; also A9, A10 |
| Loading | The insurer's markup above expected loss for costs, profit and uncertainty. | A10 |
| Local vertical (LVLH) frame | A frame with axes pointing toward Earth and along the orbit track, which turns once per orbit and defines the top and bottom of the swing. | A2 |
| localhost | The name for 'this same computer' in a web address. | A12 |
| `localStorage` | A small per-site data store kept by one browser on one computer. | A12; also B9 |
| Locked brummel | A splice with an interlock that stops the joined lines pulling apart. | A6 |
| Locking | Marking a decision or number as fixed so that later work must treat it as settled. | B8 |
| Log spacing | Grid points separated by a constant multiplying factor rather than a constant step. | A9; also A11 |
| Log-linear interpolation | Interpolation along a straight line in the logarithm of the input rather than the input itself. | A11 |
| Logarithm / log scale | log₁₀(x) is the power of ten giving x; on a log scale equal distances mean equal ratios. | B1 |
| Logarithmic colour scale | A colour mapping in which equal ratios of the value (1 to 10, 10 to 100) get equal colour steps. | B6 |
| Longitude of the ascending node (Ω) | The angle from the equinox direction to the ascending node, measured in the reference plane. | B3 |
| Lorentz force | The sideways force a magnetic field puts on a moving charge or current, F = I\*l x B for a wire. | A5 |
| Loss budget | Extra delta-v a rocket must supply to overcome gravity, drag and steering losses (1.2 km/s in leg_cost.py). | A10 |
| Loud failure | Stopping with a visible error instead of silently using default values. | A12 |
| `low_departure_c3` / `high_departure_c3` | Screening statuses for a best sampled departure C3 at or below 25 km²/s², or above it; a departure-energy screen only. | B4; also B6 |
| LOX | Liquid oxygen. | A4 |
| LR-001 | Skyhook's splice literature review (docs/research/lr001_splice_literature.md), the source for the \~90% eye-splice efficiency and several creep figures. | A6 |
| Lumped-mass (bead-and-spring) model | The point beads a continuous tether is split into for simulation. | A5; also A7 |
| M5 (PIPD) | A rigid-rod polymer fibre related to PBO, about 5.3 GPa, with limited availability; a VM-001 'watch item'. | A6 |
| Mach number | Speed divided by the local speed of sound. | A1; also A2, A3, A4, A10 |
| Machine epsilon (machine precision) | The gap between 1 and the next representable 64-bit floating-point number, 2⁻⁵² ≈ 2.22e-16. | A7; also B5, B8 |
| Magic number | A value in a calculation with no stated source. | A1 |
| Magnetic field (B) | A region where moving charges feel a sideways force, measured in tesla. | A5 |
| Magnitude (brightness) | A logarithmic, backwards brightness scale on which 5 magnitudes is a factor of 100 in light. | B4; also B9 |
| Magnitude (of a vector) | The size, or length, of a vector. | A2; also B2 |
| main (branch) | The branch a project treats as official; in this guide it means origin/main. | A1; also A11, A12, B1, B12 |
| Main thread | The browser thread that runs the page's own code, where Aster assigns feasibility verdicts. | B7; also B9 |
| Make-or-buy | The choice between developing your own vehicle (NRE plus lower recurring cost) and buying flights from a provider. | A10 |
| Marching squares | An algorithm that traces contours by checking each square of four neighbouring cells and interpolating where the level crosses its edges. | B6 |
| Margin (budget allowance) | A safety allowance added to the ΔV budget for things the model leaves out. | B1; also B7 |
| Margin (validation) | The bar divided by the measured bound. | B8 |
| Marginal cost | What one more flight or kilogram costs the operator, as opposed to the price charged. | A4; also A9 |
| Markdown | The plain-text formatting language that .md files are written in. | A11 |
| Marker | A deliberate minimum-size visibility aid drawn over a body too small to see, labelled as such. | B9 |
| Market | The set of buyers and sellers for one kind of good; for Skyhook the good is delta-v sold per kilogram delivered to a destination orbit. | A10 |
| Market capacity (insurance) | How much risk the insurance market can take on one object. | A10 |

| Mass | The amount of matter in an object, which is also how hard it is to accelerate, measured in kg. | A2; also A3 |

| Matrix | Here, a 4 by 4 table of numbers that rotates, moves or projects points. | B9 |
| Max error | The largest error over the tested points; the worst case on what was tested. | B8 |
| Maximum performance / bookable | The most a rocket can lift flown flat out, versus what the standard \$74M plan covers (up to 5.5 t to GTO for Falcon 9). | A4 |

| MDL-001 | The unmerged momentum draw ledger (physics/momentum_ledger.py and physics/MOMENTUM_LEDGER_FINDINGS.md on claude/creative-momentum-draw-ledger), source of the carry-aware release model M2. | A3; also A5 |
| Mean (expected value) | The balance point, or long-run average, of a distribution. | A8 |
| Mean anomaly (M) | An angle that grows uniformly with time at rate n, 0 at perihelion, measuring the elapsed fraction of the orbit. | B3 |
| Mean motion (n, orbital angular rate) | An orbit's average angular rate, 2π divided by the period, or √(μ/a³); about 0.0010824 rad/s for the Rev A hub at 610 km. | A2; also A7, B3, B4 |
| Mean radius | Earth's average radius, 6,371 km, used by R_EARTH_KM in physics/skyhook_physics.py. | A1; also A3, A11 |
| Measured bound | The largest error actually observed on a stated sample. | B8 |
| Median (P50) | The middle value of sorted outcomes. | A8 |
| Megagram (Mg) | 10⁶ grams, equal to one tonne. | A1; also A4 |
| Megajoule (MJ) | One million joules; 1 km²/s² of specific energy is 1 MJ/kg. | A4; also A5, A9 |

| Megawatt (MW) | One million watts. | A5 |

| Mesh (3D graphics) | A 3D shape built from many small triangles. | A12 |
| Mesh (model resolution) | How finely the model cuts the cable, here the node count. | A7 |

| Milliarcsecond (mas) | One thousandth of an arcsecond; 17 mas is about 5×10⁻⁶ degrees. | B2 |
| Millihertz (mHz) | One thousandth of a cycle per second. | A7 |
| Minification | Removing whitespace and line breaks from a file without changing its meaning. | B9 |

| Minor Planet Center (MPC) | The clearing house that collects small-body observations from observatories worldwide (from memory, verify). | B4 |
| Miss distance | How close two objects come at a conjunction. | A10 |

| Mitigation | The planned response to a risk. | A10 |

| Motional EMF | The voltage v\*B\*l that builds along a conductor moving through a magnetic field. | A5 |

| MOU (memorandum of understanding) | A non-binding agreement between parties. | A10 |
| MP-001 | Skyhook's market-pricing research pass (docs/research/mp001_market_pricing.md), a source for prices, energy per kilogram and the proposed ST-002 creep test. | A1; also A4, A5, A6, A9, A10, A11, C1 |
| MPCORB E/D/F flags | Letters that can replace the U digit in the MPC's orbit file (E eccentricity assumed, D double designation, F both); SBDB-sourced data cannot contain them. | B4 |
| `mulberry32` | The small seeded PRNG used in grade.mjs so that the bootstrap intervals are byte-reproducible. | B11 |
| Multi-agent audit | Three independent AI reviews (mathematician, adversary, architect) of math code before deploy, then a reconciliation. | B1; also B12 |
| Multi-page app | A site built from several HTML entry points, each with its own bundle graph. | B9 |
| Multibody | Made of many connected parts that move relative to each other. | A7 |
| Mutation check | Deliberately breaking production code to confirm a test turns red, then restoring it. | B12 |
| Mutation score | Killed mutants divided by total minus equivalent mutants, a general measure of test strength. | B12 |
| MXER | Momentum-Exchange / Electrodynamic Reboost, an early-2000s NASA tether architecture that the project cites at architecture level only. | A5; also A10 |
| NAIF IDs | Numeric body codes (10 Sun, 399 Earth, 499 Mars, 599 Jupiter, 699 Saturn) used by NASA's navigation software and stored in bodies.ts. | B2 |
| NaN | 'Not a Number', the result of undefined arithmetic such as 0/0. | B1; also B8, B10 |
| Natural frequency | A frequency at which a structure vibrates freely when disturbed. | A7 |
| Natural logarithm (ln) | The inverse of exp: ln(eˣ) = x. | A1; also A4, A6 |
| Near and far planes | The minimum and maximum distances the camera draws, whose ratio limits depth precision. | B9 |
| Near-Earth asteroid (NEA) | A near-Earth object that is an asteroid, not a comet. | B3; also B9, C1 |

| Nesting | Placing an object or array inside another, which makes a JSON file a tree. | A11 |
| Net cash flow | Money in minus money out in one year. | A9 |
| Net force | The vector sum of all forces acting on an object. | A2 |
| Net present value (NPV) | Future cash flows converted to today's money at a stated yearly discount rate. | A1; also A8, A9 |
| New Shepard | Blue Origin's suborbital tourist rocket (from memory, verify), called a \~Mach 3 ballistic hopper in LEG_COST_FINDINGS.md. | A4 |
| Newton (N) | The SI unit of force, kg·m/s². | A1; also A2, A4, A6 |
| Newton's cannonball | Newton's thought experiment of firing a ball sideways from a very tall mountain ever faster until it falls all the way around the planet: an orbit (from memory, verify). | A3 |
| Newton's first law | An object keeps its straight-line, constant-speed motion unless a net force acts on it. | A2 |
| Newton's law of universal gravitation | F = G·M·m/r², the attraction between two masses, with r measured between their centres. | A3; also B3 |
| Newton's method | An iterative root-finder that follows the tangent line to where it crosses zero at each step. | B3; also B5, B8 |
| Newton's second law | Net force equals mass times acceleration (F = m a), or more generally the rate of change of momentum. | A2 |
| Newton's third law | Forces come in equal and opposite pairs acting on two different bodies. | A2; also A4, A5 |
| NHATS | NASA's study of human-accessible near-Earth asteroid targets, whose criteria Slice 20 relies on (expansion from memory, verify). | B3; also B12 |
| NHST | Null-hypothesis significance testing: deciding yes/no on whether data are surprising under H0. | B11 |
| NIAC | NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts, which funded HASTOL (expansion from memory, verify). | A4 |
| No-LEO stress tester | Skyhook's canonical strategy simulator, tools/sims/skyhook_no_leo_stress_test.jsx; skyhook-sim.jsx only re-exports it. | A1; also A4, A5, A8, A12 |
| NOAA | The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, which licenses commercial remote sensing (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Nodal precession | The slow swing of an inclined orbit's plane around Earth's spin axis caused by J2; about −6.38° per day at 6,981 km and 28.5°, a 56.4-day cycle. | C1 |
| Node | One of the point masses in the lumped-mass tether models. | A2; also A7 |
| `node --test` | The test runner built into Node.js (built in since Node 18, from memory, verify). | B12 |
| Node.js | A program that runs JavaScript outside a web browser. | A1; also A7, A12, B9, B12 |
| `noindex` | A page instruction asking search engines not to list the page. | B9 |
| Nominal rate | The quoted rate, which includes expected inflation. | A9 |

| npm | The JavaScript package registry and the installer that comes with Node.js; npm run &lt;name&gt; runs a script listed in package.json. | B1; also B10, B12 |
| `npm ci` | An npm command that installs dependencies exactly as pinned in package-lock.json and runs the prepare script (from memory, verify). | B12 |
| npx | The npm command that downloads a package and runs it in one step (from memory, verify). | B1 |
| NRE (non-recurring engineering) | The one-time development cost of a vehicle or system. | A4; also A9, A10, C1 |
| NTIA | The National Telecommunications and Information Administration, which manages US government spectrum (from memory, verify). | A10 |
| Null | JSON's 'no value'; in rev_a.json it means unknown, not zero. | A1; also A11, A12 |

| `package.json` | The manifest that names a JavaScript package and lists its version, scripts, dependencies and published files. | B10 |

| Port (code) | A line-by-line rewrite of a program in another language. | A7; also A11, A12 |
| Port (network) | A numbered network 'door' on a computer, e.g. 8000 for Python's web server. | A12 |
| Position (position vector) | Where an object is, measured as a vector from a chosen origin. | A2; also B2, B5 |
| Position-based constraint method | A simulation technique that keeps segment lengths fixed by nudging positions and then recomputes velocities from the movement. | A7 |
| Potentially hazardous asteroid (PHA) | An asteroid with Earth MOID &lt;= 0.05 AU and H &lt;= 22 (from memory, verify); Aster copies SBDB's flag. | B3; also B4 |
| Power | The rate of doing work or delivering energy, P = dW/dt = F\*v. | A5 |
| Power-chain efficiency | The fraction of purchased electricity that ends up as useful orbital energy; 0.15 in the conservative case. | A1; also A4, A5, A9 |
| Powered hold | A catch that holds the match for a window by cancelling a_rel with vehicle thrust or a tip-side line; the branch glossary calls it an 'active hold' (unmerged branch). | A8 |
| Pre-registration | Publishing the questions, scenarios, metrics, grading rules and analysis plan before any data are collected. | B11 |
| Pre-research | Measuring inputs and reading literature before any decision is locked. | B1; also B12 |
| Pre-strain | Building each segment already stretched so it carries the rigid-rotation tension at t = 0. | A7 |
| Preact | A small UI library with React's component and virtual-DOM model, used for Aster's panels and pages. | B9 |
| Precession | The slow wobble of Earth's spin axis (about 26,000-year cycle), which changes the equator's orientation over time and is why frames are frozen at an epoch. | B2; also B7 |
| Precision | How finely a number is stated. | A1; also B1 |
| Prefix (metric prefix) | A word or symbol that multiplies a unit by a power of ten, such as kilo (10³) or giga (10⁹). | A1; also B1 |
| Premium | The payment made for insurance cover. | A10 |
| `prepublishOnly` | An npm script that runs automatically before npm publish; Aster's runs check-publish-clean.mjs to block publishing from a dirty worktree. | B10 |
| Present value (PV) | What a future amount is worth today after discounting. | A9 |
| Price | What each unit costs, measured here in dollars per kilogram (\$/kg). | A9; also A10 |
| Price elasticity of demand | The percentage change in quantity bought divided by the percentage change in price; elastic if E &lt; -1, inelastic if -1 &lt; E &lt; 0. | A10 |
| Price per kilogram (\$/kg) | A launch price divided by the payload mass the rocket can carry to a stated destination. | A4 |
| Price umbrella | The room under a substitute's price within which a seller can set its price and still win; in the repo, the GTO-over-LEO premium launch customers already pay. | A1; also A10 |

| Print stylesheet | CSS written for printing to paper or PDF, like materials/style.css with @page Letter. | A12 |
| Priors (audit lenses) | The deliberately different starting assumptions of the mathematician, adversarial and architect reviewers. | B8 |
| Probability | A number from 0 (never) to 1 (always) giving how likely an event is, read either as a long-run frequency or a degree of belief. | A8 |
| Probability density function (PDF) | A curve whose area between two points gives the probability that a continuous variable lands between them. | A8 |
| Probability of collision (Pc) | The chance two objects hit, given tracking uncertainty; many operators maneuver near 1 in 10,000 (from memory, verify). | A10 |

| Profit / loss | Revenue minus cost; a negative profit is a loss. | A9 |

| Program | A text file of instructions run top to bottom. | A12 |
| Project site | A GitHub Pages site served under a path named after its repository. | B9 |
| Projection | The step that maps 3D camera-space points to the 2D image, making far things smaller. | B9 |
| Promise | A placeholder for a value or error that will arrive later, such as the result of a download. | B9 |
| Prompt form / paraphrase | The wording of a scenario: the ORIGINAL or one of two rewordings (P1, P2) used to test sensitivity to wording. | B11 |

| Protocol | An agreed format and order of messages that both sides must follow. | B10 |
| Provenance | The recorded chain of where a number or file came from: which inputs, which code or commit, and when. | A9; also A11, A12, B1, B4, B8 |
| Provenance class | A label on a pinned cell naming the kind of evidence behind it, such as oracle-anchored, aster-self-consistent or tool-output-pinned. | B8 |
| Pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) | A fixed recipe that produces numbers that look random but are fully determined by a starting seed. | A8; also B11 |
| PTA (provenance transmission) | Passes when at least one source is cited and every cited source matches a real provenance id, path or invoked tool from the run. | B11 |
| Pull request (PR) | A GitHub page asking to merge one branch into another, showing the diff, check results and discussion. | B12 |
| Push / fetch / pull | Push uploads your commits to a remote, fetch downloads its commits, and pull fetches and then merges them. | A12; also B1, B12 |

| `pytest.approx` | Tolerant equality for numbers in a test. | A12 |
| `pytest.raises` / `pytest.warns` | Checks that pass only if the code raises a given error or issues a given warning. | A12 |
| `PytestRemovedIn10Warning` | pytest's warning that class-scoped fixtures written as methods are scheduled to stop working in pytest 10. | A12 |
| Python | The programming language used for the project's models and tests. | A12 |
| Quadratic convergence | The property that the number of correct digits roughly doubles with each step near the answer. | B3 |
| Quadratic token growth | Input tokens grow roughly with the square of tool calls because every turn resends the whole conversation. | B11 |
| `qualityRank` | Aster's own 0–1 orbit-quality score built from the U code and the data arc; it is computed for every body but used by no UI. | B4 |
| Quantity (envelope leaf) | Aster's numeric leaf in an envelope: a finite value with non-empty units, plus an optional frame, confidence and sourceIds. | B1; also B10, C1 |
| Quirks mode | An old browser compatibility mode used for pages without a doctype. | A12 |
| RAAN (right ascension of the ascending node) | The angle, measured along the equator from a fixed sky direction, to where an Earth orbit crosses the equator going north; J2 makes it drift. | C1 |
| Radial | Pointing along the line from Earth's centre. | A7 |
| Radial / tangential velocity | The velocity components along the line from the central body and sideways within the orbital plane. | B5 |
| Radian | The angle at which arc length equals radius; a full circle is 2π radians. | A1; also A2 |
| Radius basis | The Earth radius a computed value assumes; rev_a.json mixes a 6,981 km (mean) and a 6,988 km (equatorial) CoM radius. | A2; also A3, A5, A11 |
| Ramp | The slow start of output after operations begin. | A9 |
| Random variable | A quantity whose value comes from a chance process; discrete if it takes countable values, continuous if it can take any value in a range. | A8 |
| Range cost | The fee for using a launch range and its safety services (\$250,000 floor in leg_cost.py). | A4 |
| Range safety | Keeping people on the ground and aircraft clear of a vehicle's flight corridors and abort footprints. | A10; also B7 |
| Ratchet (test) | A test that fails only on new problems beyond a pinned baseline, so the count can go down but not up. | A11 |
| Rate (insurance) | Premium divided by insured value. | A10 |
| Ratio | One quantity divided by another. | A1; also B1 |
| Rayleigh distribution | The distribution of the length of a 2-D error whose two components are independent normals with the same sigma; CDF 1 - exp(-r^2/(2 sigma^2)). | A8 |
| RB-001 | The 'Rev B' document, which exists only on claude.ai, not in the repository (handoff.md open item 4). | A1; also A4, A9, A10, A11 |
| Re-anchor epoch | The instant (2026-05-01 00:00 TDB) at which most catalog orbits were reset from Horizons data. | B1 |

| React | A JavaScript library that builds pages from component functions. | A12 |
| Read as input | Used by another program as a source of numbers, as finance/reboost_bound.py uses the MXER draft. | A11 |
| Real rate | A discount or interest rate measured above inflation, matching cash flows in constant prices. | A9 |
| Reboost | Restoring the tether's orbital energy after each throw. | A4; also A10 |

| Recall | The fraction of real misquotes a checker catches. | A11 |
| recharts | A React chart library the stress-test JSX imports. | A12 |
| Recon | A read-only investigation of the repository or a problem, often by a fresh agent session. | B1; also B2, B12 |
| Reconciliation (agreement check) | Showing that two separate calculations agree within a stated tolerance. | A9; also A12 |
| Reconciliation (audit pass) | The fourth audit pass that merges the lens findings, removes duplicates, ranks them HIGH/MED/LOW and judges the arguments rather than the artifact. | B8 |

| Recurring cost | The cost incurred on every flight. | A4; also A10 |

| Refresh rate | How many times per second a display redraws, for example 60 Hz. | B9 |
| Refusal | A first-class result with value null and a code, reason and what_would_help, used when the tool cannot answer. | B1; also B10, C1 |

| Registry (CA-001) | A table of canon claim specs tying each quantity to its rev_a path or function, units, tier and rung. | A11 |

| Relative and absolute thresholds | Segmentation at T = liveMin + 5 (each body's own valley structure) or at T = 25 (the shared screening boundary). | B6 |
| Relative change | (new − old) ÷ old. | A1 |
| Relative error | \|actual − expected\| ÷ \|expected\|. | A1; also A11, A12, B1, B5, B7, B8, B11 |

| Relative step tolerance | Stop when the change in x is smaller than a fixed fraction of \|x\|. | B8 |
| Relative tip acceleration (a_rel, felt load at the catch) | The tether tip's acceleration relative to a body coasting freely at the same point, v_tip^2/L plus a gravity-gradient term: about 20.34 m/s^2 (2.07 g) at Rev A, which is also what the payload's accelerometer reads at the catch, 4% above canon's 1.99 g (named in the unmerged catch-window study, CW-001). | A2; also A8 |
| Relative velocity | The velocity of one object as seen from another object or frame. | A2; also A5 |

| Remote / origin | The copy of the repository on a server such as GitHub; origin is its usual name. | A12; also B12 |
| Renderer | The code (in Aster, a Three.js object) that draws the scene into the page. | A12; also B9 |
| Rendezvous | Bringing two bodies to the same place at the same velocity; for Aster, matching the asteroid's velocity on arrival, which costs \|v∞,arr\|. | A1; also A5, B1, B6, B7 |

| Repo root | The project's top folder. | A12 |

| Reproducibility | Getting the identical result when a calculation is re-run, which a fixed seed provides. | A8 |
| Request / response / notification | A JSON-RPC message that asks for something; the reply that carries the same id with a result or error; and a request with no id that expects no reply. | B10 |
| Research question (RQ) | A question that asks how much or how often, answered by estimating a rate. | B11 |

| Rest length (L0) | The unstretched length of a segment. | A7 |

| Right ascension | The angle of a sky direction measured around the celestial equator. | B7; also C1 |

| Settle | For a promise, to finish by either succeeding with a value or failing with an error. | B9 |

| Sidereal day | One rotation of Earth relative to the stars, about 86,164 s (from memory, verify). | A1; also A2, A3, A4, B7 |

| Skyhook / rotovator (rotating momentum-exchange tether) | A long orbiting cable that spins end over end about its centre of mass, so its tips swing down to catch payloads and up to throw them; "skyhook" and "rotovator" are interchangeable names. | A1; also A2, C1 |
| Slack | The state of a cable segment that is not stretched and therefore carries no tension. | A7 |
| Slice | A numbered piece of work that ships one working capability end to end. | B1; also B2, B9, B11, B12 |
| Slug | A lower-case identifier made by turning every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 into one dash and trimming end dashes, as in falcon-heavy-expendable. | B10 |
| Software licence (MIT, GPL, MPL-2.0) | Reuse terms: MIT is permissive, GPL requires derived works to stay GPL, MPL-2.0 applies copyleft per file (from memory, verify). | B5 |
| Solar System Barycentre (SSB) | The centre of mass of the whole Solar System, the origin of barycentric frames; the Sun's centre is 0.13–1.67 solar radii from it. | B1; also B2 |
| Solid fibre area | The area of actual fibre in a cable (mass per metre divided by density), not the outer circle of a rope that is partly air. | A6 |
| SOM (serviceable obtainable market) | The part of the market you can realistically win. | A10 |
| Sortie | One flight of the leg vehicle. | A4; also A9, A10 |
| Sounding rocket | A small research rocket that flies up and falls straight back. | A4 |
| Source gap | UX run P1's term for a feature missing from the MCP source itself (Slice 18's fidelity tiers), so republishing the package alone would not deliver it, unlike a republish gap. | C1 |
| SourceRef | One provenance entry, of kind repo, external or computation, naming where a number came from and its class; shipped tools emit only repo refs. | B10 |
| Space elevator | A static cable anchored at the equator and reaching past geostationary altitude; not the same as a skyhook. | A1 |
| Space situational awareness (SSA) | The tracking and prediction of objects in orbit. | A10 |
| Spacer | An empty element as tall as the whole list, which keeps the scrollbar truthful in a virtualised list. | B9 |
| Span | The width of a tornado bar, \|output at high - output at low\|. | A8 |
| Spearman rank correlation | A statistic from −1 to +1 measuring whether one quantity tends to rise in rank as another does. | B3; also B4 |
| Specific angular momentum | h = r × v (m²/s), a vector perpendicular to the plane of an orbit. | B2 |
| Specific impulse (Isp) | A rocket-engine efficiency rating in seconds; Isp × g₀ gives the exhaust velocity. | A2; also A4, A5, B1, B6, B7 |
| Specific orbital energy (ε) | Kinetic plus gravitational potential energy per kilogram, ε = v²/2 − μ/r = −μ/(2a), in km²/s² (equal to MJ/kg); negative means bound. | A3; also A4, A5, B3, B5, B6, C1 |
| Specific power | Watts of output per kilogram of solar array, bracketed at 50–100 W/kg in Skyhook's reboost sizing. | A5 |
| Specific strength | Tensile strength divided by density, an energy per mass (3.72 MJ/kg for Zylon in Rev A). | A1; also A6 |
| [Speculative] | The confidence label for an informed guess; Skyhook's rule bars such values from the financial base case. | A1; also A4, A11, B1, C1 |
| Speed | The magnitude of velocity, a scalar. | A2; also A3, B2 |
| Sphere of influence | The region around a body (a planet, or the Moon) inside which its own gravity is the better centre for computing a path. | A3; also B6 |
| Spin angular momentum | The angular momentum of the tether rotating about its own centre, about 7.39e13 kg\*m^2/s for Rev A. | A5 |
| Spin period | The time for the tether to turn once about its CoM relative to the fixed stars, 13.4 minutes in Rev A. | A3 |
| Spin-up | Getting the tether rotating in the first place, which Skyhook's repository describes only in words (weeks of electrodynamic torque and/or tip thrusters). | A2 |
| Spiral of death | A runaway in which one slow frame forces many physics steps that make the next frame slow too. | A7 |
| SPK-ID | JPL's numeric identifier for a body (Eros is 20000433 in the fixture). | B4 |
| Spot check | Recomputing a sample of stored results to confirm they match the model. | A11 |
| Spreadsheet | A grid of cells addressed by column letter and row number. | A11 |
| ST-001 | Skyhook's first, cheap splice test plan ('the kitchen test', docs/st001_splice_test.md) on 1.75 mm HMPE throw line; paused, with no data yet. | A1; also A6, A8 |
| ST-002 | A creep test proposed in MP-001: hang two coupons of the ST-001 line at 20% and 40% of break and measure stretch weekly; a proposal only. | A6 |
| Stability limit | The largest value of omega times dt for which an integrator does not blow up on an oscillation (about 2.83 for RK4, 2 for Verlet; from memory, verify). | A7 |
| Stage (git) | To mark a changed file for inclusion in the next commit. | B1 |
| Staging / stage | Building a rocket as a stack of smaller rockets and dropping each empty stage so its dead mass is not carried further. | A4 |
| Stale | Describes a cached or generated value whose inputs have changed since it was computed. | A11 |
| Staleness | The time between an element epoch and the common epoch JD 2461161.5 (2026-05-01 TDB). | B4 |
| Staleness test | A test that rebuilds a committed output and requires it to still match. | A12 |

| Standard error (SE) | The typical size of sampling error; for a probability, sqrt(p(1-p)/N). | A8; also B11 |

| Starship | SpaceX's fully reusable super-heavy rocket, still in development, refuelled in orbit by tanker flights (from memory, verify). | A10 |

| Statics | The study of balanced, unchanging loads. | A7 |
| Stationkeeping | A fixed allowance of small burns for staying with the target. | B1; also B7, C1 |
| Statistical power | The probability that a study detects a real effect of a given size. | B11 |
| Status taxonomy | The fixed list of labels a component returns to say what happened (e.g. ok, no_solution, stall). | B5 |
| `STATUS.md` | Aster's current-state record of slices, open problems and recorded test results; it must be refreshed from commands to stay true, and at cec19e7 it was 39 commits behind main. | B1; also B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B8, B9, B11, B12 |
| Stdin / stdout / stderr | A process's input stream, its output stream, and its side channel for warnings and diagnostics. | B10 |
| Stdio | Communication through a program's standard input and output streams, like two programs joined by a pipe. | B1; also B10 |
| Steady state | The assumption that every later year repeats the last modelled year. | A9 |
| Steady tugs, sudden kicks, non-gravitational forces | The three causes of drift: continuous planetary pulls, close-approach deflections, and forces such as outgassing and the Yarkovsky effect. | B3 |

| Stiffness (k) | The spring constant of a particular piece, k = E·A/L0, so long pieces are softer than short ones. | A6; also A7 |
